Pick by what your sales team acts on: company guesses or verified people

tools.name: Breezy HR
tools.what_it_does: Recruiting and applicant tracking made simple. Post jobs to 50+ boards, manage candidates on a visual pipeline, and automate scheduling and screening.
tools.pricing: A genuinely permanent free Bootstrap plan (one open position, unlimited users); paid runs about $157/mo (Startup) to $439/mo (Business) on annual billing — higher month-to-month — plus a custom-quoted Pro tier. Every paid tier includes unlimited users and positions (2026).
tools.honest_knock: The jump from free (one position) to the first paid tier is steep if you only hire occasionally — the free plan is genuinely usable, so live in it until you're filling several roles at once.
tools.best_for: small teams hiring for a few roles at once that want a visual, drag-and-drop pipeline without enterprise-ATS pricing
tools.skip_if: you hire once or twice a year — the free single-position plan is plenty, and the paid jump only pays off with concurrent open roles

tools.name: Brevo
tools.what_it_does: Email marketing, SMS and CRM in one platform. Design campaigns, automate follow-ups and manage contacts so you can nurture leads and customers from a single hub.
tools.pricing: Free forever (300 emails/day, unlimited contacts); paid Starter from about $9/mo and Business from $18/mo, scaling by monthly send volume rather than contact count (2026).
tools.honest_knock: Charging by sends rather than contacts is genuinely cheaper for big lists you email infrequently — but the free daily cap and add-on fees mean high-frequency senders should model their real send volume first.
tools.best_for: businesses with large contact lists who email selectively and want to pay by send volume, not list size
tools.skip_if: you email your whole list daily — the per-send model can flip from cheap to costly at high frequency

tools.name: Bright Data
tools.what_it_does: The web data platform trusted by enterprises. Collect public web data at scale with proxies, ready-made datasets and scraping APIs — fuel for your market research and AI projects.
tools.pricing: Usage-based (re-verified 16 Jul 2026, mid-sale): residential proxies list $5/GB with a 50%-off promo showing $2.50/GB; datacenter from $0.90/IP and ISP from $1.30/IP. API side: Unlocker, Crawl and SERP APIs from $1/1k requests (free tiers available), Scraper APIs $0.75/1k records (sale; list $1), Data Firehose $0.20/1k, Datasets from $250/100k records; managed offerings from $1,500/mo (Managed Data Acquisition) and Retail Insights from $2,000/mo.
tools.honest_knock: This is enterprise-grade web data infrastructure at enterprise-grade prices — the per-GB meter looks small until you multiply by real scraping volume, and the committed tiers only pay off if your usage is steady. The bigger honest note is compliance: Bright Data is strict about KYC and use-cases (a feature, not a bug), and whatever you collect still has to respect the target sites' terms and applicable law. Budget legal thought alongside the gigabytes.
tools.best_for: data teams and enterprises with real, ongoing web-data needs (pricing intelligence, market research) that justify committed volume and pass use-case vetting
tools.skip_if: you need occasional small scrapes (Browse.ai-class tools or datasets are far cheaper), or your use-case wouldn't survive a compliance review
compare_with: the premium proxy/data peers — compare effective per-GB at your committed volume and the quality on your specific target sites

tools.name: Browse.ai
tools.what_it_does: No-code web scraping and data extraction. Turn any website into an automated data pipeline or spreadsheet automatically.
tools.pricing: Credit-metered (2026): Free ~50 credits/mo (2 sites); Personal about $19/mo annual (12,000 credits/yr, 5 sites); Professional ~$69/mo annual (60,000 credits, 10 sites); Premium custom (600k+ credits, managed). A credit ≈ 10 extracted rows; premium sites cost more credits.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest realities of no-code scraping: credits burn faster than expected (row counts, screenshots and 'premium' sites all multiply the meter — monitor a big site daily and do the math first), and scrapers break when sites redesign — robots need maintenance, which is your time even when the tool is no-code. Also check the terms of the sites you monitor; 'technically possible' and 'permitted' aren't the same thing.
tools.best_for: ops, research and growth teams that want to monitor competitors, prices or listings and pipe structured web data into sheets without writing scrapers
tools.skip_if: you need one-off extractions (free tools or a VA are cheaper), or mission-critical pipelines where you'd rather own the code than rent the robot
compare_with: close scraping platforms — Apify is more developer-oriented; compare credit math on YOUR row volumes and site list

tools.name: BuddyPunch
tools.what_it_does: Time clock and employee time tracking for hourly teams. Track hours, breaks, PTO and overtime with GPS and photo punch-in, and export payroll-ready reports.
tools.pricing: Per-user plus a base fee: Starter about $5.49/user/mo, Pro $6.99, Enterprise $11.99, each with a roughly $19/mo base fee (2026). GPS and scheduling are add-ons on lower tiers and a payroll add-on costs extra. 14-day trial, no card.
tools.honest_knock: That flat $19 base fee makes it pricey for very small teams — at three or four users the base fee dominates the bill, so it's better value once you're past a handful of employees.
tools.best_for: small-to-mid teams that need straightforward employee time tracking with GPS and payroll-ready exports
tools.skip_if: you're a team of two or three — the fixed base fee makes the per-head cost sting until you scale up

tools.name: BugHerd
tools.what_it_does: Visual bug tracking and website feedback. Let clients and teams point-and-click to report issues right on the page, turned into trackable tasks.
tools.pricing: Standard about $42/mo (5 members), Studio ~$67/mo (10), Premium ~$125/mo (25), plus custom Enterprise — all with unlimited projects and unlimited client users; annual billing runs $500/$800/$1,500 per year (two months free), extra members $6.60/user/mo. Free trial (re-verified 2026-07-19).
tools.honest_knock: The per-team-member tiers are the thing to size honestly: your clients report for free as guests, but everyone on your side who works the feedback needs a seat, so a growing agency steps up tiers. It's deliberately a visual-feedback layer, not a full project-management or dev-issue tracker — most teams run it alongside Jira/Trello rather than instead of. The new MCP feature is genuinely interesting but currently beta: treat AI-agents-triaging-your-feedback as a bonus to evaluate, not the reason to buy.
tools.best_for: web agencies and site teams that want clients to point-and-click feedback directly on the page — and, new in 2026, want AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor and others) to read, triage and action that feedback via BugHerd's MCP server, free in beta
tools.skip_if: you don't work with external clients or website revisions (a plain issue tracker is enough), or you need deep dev-workflow tracking that belongs in Jira
compare_with: close visual-feedback rivals — BugHerd currently stands out with its MCP/AI-agent integration; compare per-seat costs at your team size

tools.name: Buzz.ai
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered outbound platform: prompt it and it finds intent-ready buyers, writes multichannel sequences and books the meetings — per-seat plans with monthly credit allowances and a free start.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 16 Jul 2026) Core $125/mo per seat with 500 credits/seat/mo — a launch offer runs $75/mo for the first 3 months (and $75/mo per seat billed annually); AI Employee $795/mo per seat with 5,000 credits/seat/mo, and the pricing page itself warns it ‘moves to $1,000/mo soon’; custom tier via sales. Free start available.
tools.honest_knock: Two meters run at once: seats AND credits — the $125 seat includes 500 credits a month, and real outbound volume means credit packages on top, so budget past the sticker. Watch the launch math too: $75 is a 3-month teaser that steps up to $125, and the top tier openly signposts a rise from $795 to $1,000 — decide on the post-rise price, not the promo. And the honest fundamental for any AI-SDR: it only books meetings as good as your list and offer, so keep a human reviewing what goes out in your name.
tools.best_for: GTM teams that want AI to run outbound end-to-end — prompt-driven prospecting of intent-ready buyers, multichannel sequences and meeting booking without adding SDR headcount
tools.skip_if: you send low-volume, hand-crafted outreach (per-seat-plus-credits is overkill), or you're not ready to QA an AI that writes to your market on your behalf
compare_with: Reply.io is mature multichannel sequencing you drive yourself and lemlist leads on deliverability and personalization — Buzz.ai's pitch is the autonomous AI-SDR layer that does the driving for you

tools.name: Bybit
tools.what_it_does: Trade crypto with deep liquidity — derivatives, spot and EU-compliant infrastructure.
tools.pricing: No subscription — per-trade fees (2026): spot base 0.1% maker/taker for non-VIP; derivatives around 0.02% maker / 0.055% taker; options ~0.03%. VIP tiers (by volume or balance) cut rates toward zero, with maker rebates at the top.
tools.honest_knock: Derivatives are the draw and the danger: leverage cuts both ways, and funding rates on perpetuals are a real recurring cost the fee table doesn't show. Regulation-wise, check what Bybit may offer in YOUR jurisdiction before funding an account — availability and product range differ per country, and that's the part most fee comparisons skip.
tools.best_for: active traders who want deep liquidity, low derivatives fees and a broad product range (spot, perps, options) with volume-tiered discounts
tools.skip_if: you're a buy-and-hold beginner (a simple euro-native exchange is safer territory), or derivatives aren't available to you locally
compare_with: Bitvavo is the euro on/off-ramp specialist, Kraken the regulated all-rounder — Bybit wins on derivatives depth

tools.name: Calilio
tools.what_it_does: Modern, reliable business VoIP communications. Set up clear, automated phone menus and virtual numbers in minutes.
tools.pricing: (2026) Standard about $12/user/mo annual ($15 monthly, up to 10 users, 1 local number, ~300 free minutes); Premium ~$28/user/mo (unlimited users, live monitoring); Enterprise custom. Numbers are billed separately; calls/SMS draw from credit.
tools.honest_knock: The subscription is the platform, not the talking: numbers, minutes and SMS meter separately from a credit balance, so an active calling team's real bill sits meaningfully above the per-seat sticker — model a month of your actual call volume before comparing vendors. It's a young player in a crowded VoIP field; the price is keen, so test call quality on your real routes in the trial.
tools.best_for: startups and small teams that want a modern, affordable cloud phone system with international numbers and clean dashboards
tools.skip_if: you need a battle-tested enterprise contact center with deep integrations and SLAs, or your call volume makes metered credits unpredictable
compare_with: close low-cost VoIP rivals — compare the metered call rates on the countries you actually call, not the seat price

tools.name: CallHippo
tools.what_it_does: AI-driven business phone system. Virtual numbers in 50+ countries, power dialer, call analytics and AI agents — set up your sales and support calling in minutes. Its omnichannel inbox threads voice, WhatsApp, SMS, email, Instagram and Telegram into one conversation per customer.
tools.pricing: (2026) A Basic plan, free for the first 6 months from signup (re-verified 2026-07-31); Starter about $18/user/mo (1,000 US/CA minutes, 100 SMS), Professional ~$30 (unlimited US/CA calling), Ultimate ~$42; call-center 'Pro Suite' tiers $32-48/user/mo annual; Enterprise custom at 50+ users. AI copilot, AI voice agent and CNAM are paid add-ons.
tools.honest_knock: 'Unlimited calling' is unlimited to the US and Canada — international minutes meter separately, so teams calling Europe or Asia should price their real destinations first. The plan grid is busy (two suites, add-ons for the dialer and AI), which makes comparisons slippery: list the five features you actually need and find the cheapest tier that truly contains all five.
tools.best_for: budget-conscious sales/support teams wanting virtual numbers in 50+ countries with a free entry point and CRM integrations
tools.skip_if: your calling is mostly international at volume (metered minutes stack up), or you want one simple plan without add-on shopping
compare_with: the budget-VoIP peer group — decide on per-country call rates and which features are add-ons vs included

tools.name: CallRail
tools.what_it_does: Call tracking and marketing attribution. See which campaigns, keywords and ads drive phone calls and form leads, with recordings and analytics to prove ROI.
tools.pricing: (2026) Four plans about $50–$195/mo: Call Tracking $50, +Conversation Intelligence or +Form Tracking $100, Complete $195. Prices assume tight limits (~250 local minutes, 5 numbers, 25 SMS); overages meter (~$0.05/local minute, ~$3 per extra number). 14-day trial, no free plan.
tools.honest_knock: The headline price is a floor, not a ceiling — the included minutes, numbers and SMS are modest, so an active campaign quickly hits metered overages that meaningfully lift the bill. It's also specifically an attribution tool: it proves which marketing drives calls and leads, but it isn't a phone system or CRM, so you add it alongside those, not instead of them.
tools.best_for: marketers and agencies that need to prove which campaigns, keywords and ads drive phone calls and form leads, with recordings and multi-touch attribution
tools.skip_if: you don't run enough paid marketing to need call-level attribution, or your call volume would push overages past the value of the insight
compare_with: WhatConverts or a platform's native tracking
comparable attribution tools — compare on included minutes and how your real call volume meters

tools.name: Campaign Monitor
tools.what_it_does: Premium email marketing tailored for agencies and scaling teams. Delivers stunning templates and reliable deliverability.
tools.pricing: Contact-based (2026): for 500 contacts roughly Lite $12-13/mo (send cap ~5x contacts), Essentials $29-31/mo (unlimited sends), Premier $159-171/mo; the same tiers climb steeply with list size (Essentials at 10k contacts ≈ $89/mo). Annual billing saves ~25%.
tools.honest_knock: You pay for contacts, not sends — so a large, quiet list costs the same as a large, active one, and dormant subscribers are literally a line item. Clean your list before comparing prices anywhere. Campaign Monitor's strength is polished, agency-friendly email; its automation depth is lighter than dedicated marketing-automation platforms, so know which of the two jobs you're actually buying.
tools.best_for: brands and agencies that want beautiful, reliable email campaigns with strong templates and client-friendly management, priced per contact
tools.skip_if: you need deep behavioral automation and CRM-grade journeys (ActiveCampaign-class tools fit better), or your list is large but low-engagement — prune first
compare_with: Mailchimp is the closest general peer, ActiveCampaign wins on automation depth — compare at YOUR list size, since contact pricing diverges fast

tools.name: Campaigner
tools.what_it_does: Advanced email and SMS marketing for mid-market teams. Build automated journeys, segment audiences and run A/B tests with detailed reporting.
tools.pricing: (2026) Contact-based: Starter about $59/mo (5,000 contacts, no automation/API); Essential ~$179/mo (25k contacts, dynamic content, 1,000 SMS); Advanced ~$649/mo (100k, workflows, API); an eCommerce plan runs ~$79.95-149.95/mo. 30-day trial requires a card and auto-converts.
tools.honest_knock: Two paragraphs of fine print worth reading: automation and API only arrive at the $179 tier — the Starter plan is a sending tool, not a marketing-automation platform — and the trial auto-converts to paid if you don't actively cancel, which tells you something about the retention strategy. Contact-based pricing also means dormant subscribers bill like active ones; prune first.
tools.best_for: mid-market senders with larger lists that want mature email plus SMS workflows and are comfortable at the Essential tier and up
tools.skip_if: you're small (the useful features start at $179/mo) or you dislike card-required auto-converting trials on principle
compare_with: Campaign Monitor shares the polish, ActiveCampaign beats it on automation depth — compare at your real list size and feature floor

tools.name: Capsule
tools.what_it_does: Simple, focused CRM for small businesses. Track contacts, sales pipelines and tasks in one tidy place so nothing slips between deals and follow-ups.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free tier (250 contacts, 2 users); Starter about $21/user/mo, Growth ~$38, Advanced ~$60, Ultimate ~$75; annual saves ~15-20%. 14-day trial, no card.
tools.honest_knock: Capsule's simplicity is the product: it deliberately does less than the CRM giants, which is why small teams actually use it. The honest flip side — advanced automation, deep reporting and integrations thin out at the top tiers, and a scaling sales org can outgrow it. Buy it to finally have a CRM the team fills in; plan a migration path if you're heading toward enterprise process complexity.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want a clean, genuinely simple CRM for contacts, pipeline and tasks — one the team will actually keep updated
tools.skip_if: you need marketing automation, complex territory logic or enterprise reporting (bigger platforms exist for a reason)
compare_with: the SMB-CRM peer group — Capsule wins on calm simplicity, Pipedrive on pipeline power; pick by which your team will really use

tools.name: Carbon6
tools.what_it_does: SPS Commerce Revenue Recovery — the toolset formerly sold as Carbon6, acquired by SPS Commerce on 7 Feb 2025 and folded into spscommerce.com. Recovers retailer deductions, chargebacks and shortages for 1P suppliers across Amazon, Walmart, Target and Kroger, alongside SoStocked, ScanUnlimited and SPS Ad Performance (formerly PixelMe). Note: the 3P Amazon FBA reimbursement arm was divested on 30 Jun 2026 to an undisclosed buyer.
tools.pricing: What we can verify on the vendor's own pages today (checked 21 Jul 2026): SoStocked lists ProfitFlow at $97/mo and ProfitFlow + Inventory at "starting at" $250/mo; ScanUnlimited lists a free Limited tier, Unlimited at $720/yr and Unlimited Plus at $1,080/yr. SPS Ad Performance (the former PixelMe) publishes no price at all — it is contact-sales only. The 3P FBA-reimbursement service publishes no commission rate on its page; it is sold as a contingency arrangement (vendor claim: you pay only on money actually recovered, with the fee reversed if Amazon claws a reimbursement back), and since that business changed hands on 30 Jun 2026 we cannot verify who sets the rate now. We therefore quote no reimbursement percentage. Our previous figures — entry tools from about $49/mo, PixelMe from about $500/mo with a 6-month minimum, about 25% of recovered, and $300-500+/mo for a working stack — are withdrawn: none of them is verifiable against a live authoritative source today.
tools.honest_knock: The honest headline is no longer pricing — it's ownership. This is not a standalone vendor: SPS Commerce bought Carbon6 for roughly $210M on 7 Feb 2025 and retired the brand into spscommerce.com. Then on 30 Jun 2026 SPS announced it had sold the entire 3P (Amazon marketplace seller) revenue-recovery business for $9.5M cash, booking an estimated $20M loss, and did not name the buyer. Read those two numbers carefully, because they are not the same thing: the $210M bought the whole Carbon6 stack, while the $9.5M was the 3P arm on its own. Even so, offloading that arm at a book loss seventeen months in tells you how it performed — and it is precisely the piece we previously told you to start with. Sign-up flows still route through login.carbon6.io and the SoStocked page still links to a Carbon6 notice, so the plumbing is mid-migration. Compounding it: Reuters reported on 23 Jun 2026 that SPS itself hired Morgan Stanley to explore a sale under activist pressure, talks early and no deal assured. Buy the 1P deduction-recovery work on its merits — SPS kept it and is investing in it. For 3P reimbursements, wait until you can name the counterparty on your contract.
tools.best_for: suppliers chasing 1P deductions, chargebacks and shortages across Amazon, Walmart, Target and Kroger — the half SPS Commerce deliberately kept, and the only half with a settled owner
tools.skip_if: your job is 3P Amazon FBA reimbursements — that arm was sold on 30 Jun 2026 to an undisclosed buyer, so you cannot yet name who holds your contract, your Seller Central access or your fee
compare_with: Helium 10 is the flat-priced seller suite with published tiers; GETIDA is the independent FBA-reimbursement specialist — against a business that has changed hands twice in eighteen months, both win on the plain fact that you know who you are contracting with

tools.name: Checkr
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered background check and screening platform for hiring: fast criminal, employment and identity verification with automated adjudication and ATS integrations — speeds up onboarding while staying FCRA-compliant.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-07-23) Pay-as-you-go per report, no subscription: Basic $29.99, Essential $59.99 and Complete $94.99 per report, with Enterprise quote-only. Tenant screening is priced separately at $24.99, $34.99 and $44.99 per report, and personal checks start from $49.99. Add-ons stack on top: MVR report $9.50/check, identity verification $4.99/check, drug screening from $10/test, FACIS from $6/check and employment verification from $12.50/check. On top of that, standard third-party court and database access fees are passed through at cost with no markup, so the real cost per hire lands above the sticker price.
tools.honest_knock: The headline per-check price is rarely what you actually pay — passthrough fees vary wildly by county and search type, so budget for the effective cost, not the advertised one. It's overkill unless you hire at real volume.
tools.best_for: companies hiring hourly or gig workers at volume that need fast, API-driven, compliant background checks
tools.skip_if: you hire only a handful of people a year — a one-off check from a simpler provider costs less hassle than onboarding a screening platform

tools.name: ChemiCloud
tools.what_it_does: Lightning-fast cloud hosting with free migrations, daily backups, and 24/7 expert support. Perfect balance of performance and affordability for growing businesses.
tools.pricing: (2026) Promotional shared hosting from about $2.49/mo (free domain year one, free SSL, daily backups, 45-day money-back). Note the renewal: standard rates run roughly 3x the intro price (often ~$9.95–$14.95/mo). Reseller from ~$19.95/mo, cloud VPS from ~$29.95/mo.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is the one every budget host shares: the headline price is an introductory rate, and renewals land roughly three times higher, so judge it on the renewal cost, not the sign-up teaser. Support and performance reviews are genuinely strong for the price band, but this is shared/managed hosting — if you need serious dedicated resources or enterprise SLAs, you'll outgrow the cheap tiers. Great value to start, just enter with eyes open on renewal.
tools.best_for: small businesses, freelancers and growing sites that want fast, well-supported managed shared or WordPress hosting at a low starting price
tools.skip_if: you need enterprise-grade dedicated infrastructure and SLAs, or you'll be unhappy when the low intro rate renews at standard pricing
compare_with: comparable managed hosts — ChemiCloud competes hard on intro price and support; compare renewal rates and performance for your stack

tools.name: Circle
tools.what_it_does: Community platform for creator businesses: discussions, courses, events, memberships and messaging in one branded home — plus a no-code website builder, branded iOS/Android apps, email marketing, a member CRM, built-in payments and AI agents that answer member questions.
tools.pricing: (2026) Professional about $89/mo billed annually ($129 monthly), Business $199/mo annual, Enterprise around $419/mo annual, plus a custom Circle Plus tier for fully branded apps. On top of the subscription Circle takes a commission on every sale you make through the platform (roughly 2% on Professional, 1% on Business, 0.5% on Plus) plus standard Stripe/PayPal processing, and the Email Hub is a paid add-on around $99/mo for 10,000 contacts. 14-day free trial, but no always-free option.
tools.honest_knock: The sticker is only the entry: Circle keeps a commission on every sale on top of Stripe's processing fees, and email marketing is a separate add-on — so a monetized community's real bill runs meaningfully past the plan price. Model it at your actual sales volume before choosing a tier.
tools.best_for: creators and brands running a paid community — courses, memberships, events and discussions in one branded home, with a built-in payments stack and even branded mobile apps
tools.skip_if: you only need a casual chat space (Discord-style) or your margins are thin on high sales volume — the platform commission plus processing fees stack against you
compare_with: Skool wins on radical simplicity and flat pricing, Mighty Networks on affordable entry; Circle wins on breadth: branded apps, email, CRM, AI agents and a real payments stack

tools.name: Claude
tools.what_it_does: Anthropic's AI assistant for writing, coding, analysis and long-document work — strong reasoning and a careful, direct tone rather than an eager-to-please one. Free tier plus Pro, Max, Team and Enterprise plans, and a per-token API (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) for builders.
tools.pricing: Free tier at $0 with daily usage caps (2026); Pro at $20/mo (about $17 billed annually) lifts the limits and adds Projects; Max at $100/mo (roughly 5x Pro usage) or $200/mo (around 20x) for heavy daily users; Team from $25/seat/mo Standard (min 5 seats, $20 annually) with Premium at $125/seat adding Claude Code; Enterprise custom. The API is separate, billed per token across the Opus, Sonnet and Haiku models.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is usage limits: even on Pro you can hit a ceiling mid-session on a heavy day, and the step up to Max is a real $100 to $200 a month — you're buying headroom, not extra features. It also doesn't generate images, so if that's your main need it's the wrong tool, and its third-party plugin ecosystem is smaller than ChatGPT's.
tools.best_for: developers, writers, analysts and researchers who want best-in-class reasoning, coding and long-document work — and a model that's careful and direct rather than eager to please
tools.skip_if: you mainly need image generation or the widest third-party plugin ecosystem (a general assistant like ChatGPT fits better there), or you're a light user the free tier already covers
compare_with: ChatGPT leads on image generation and third-party plugins, Gemini on native Google Workspace integration — Claude's edge is reasoning depth, coding, long context and writing quality

tools.name: Clay
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered prospecting and outbound. Enrich leads from 75+ data sources and personalize at scale with GPT-driven copy that actually books meetings.
tools.pricing: From ~$185/mo (Launch, 2,500 credits) to ~$495/mo (Growth); a dual-currency credit system where each lookup costs credits (~$0.15–1+/lead), so waterfall enrichment can burn budget fast (2026).
tools.honest_knock: Two honest catches: a steep learning curve (expect 2–4 weeks, many teams need a dedicated Clay expert), and credits that are hard to forecast at scale. It's an enrichment engine, not a sender — you still need Instantly, Lemlist or Outreach to actually email.
tools.best_for: modern GTM and ops teams who want best-in-class waterfall enrichment and custom research workflows — and have someone to own it
tools.skip_if: you want to sign up and prospect on day one, or you can't dedicate time to learn it — the curve and credit spend frustrate casual users

tools.name: ClickUp
tools.what_it_does: The 'everything app' for project and work management. Centralize your tasks, docs, sprints, and team communication in one hub.
tools.pricing: A Free Forever plan (unlimited members, limited storage/features); Unlimited about $7/user/mo, Business $12/user/mo billed annually (higher monthly), plus custom Enterprise (2026).
tools.honest_knock: The everything-app breadth is also the downside — it's feature-dense with a real learning curve, and teams can drown in options. Powerful and cheap per seat, but only if you'll actually configure and adopt it.
tools.best_for: teams that want one highly customizable app for tasks, docs, goals and reporting and will invest in setting it up
tools.skip_if: you want something simple your team adopts in a day — ClickUp's depth becomes overwhelm for a light use case

tools.name: Clonable
tools.what_it_does: Creates a continuously-translated clone of your existing website — fast multilingual versions that stay synced as your site changes, without rebuilding it.
tools.pricing: (2026) Starts with a free trial. At research time the public pricing was JavaScript-gated and not cleanly readable; the model is a continuously-synced translated clone of your existing site, typically a monthly subscription scaling by domain and traffic. Verify current rates in-app before committing.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest caveats. First, it's a continuous subscription, not a one-time translation — you pay ongoing to keep the translated clone synced with your site. Second, it's machine translation under the hood, so quality varies by language pair; always have a native speaker spot-check high-stakes pages. (Public pricing was gated at research time — confirm current tiers yourself.)
tools.best_for: businesses that want a fast, continuously-updated translated version of an existing website without rebuilding it as a multilingual site
tools.skip_if: you need human-quality translation for legal, medical or brand-critical copy, or you only need a one-off translation rather than an ongoing synced clone
compare_with: Weglot is the established website-translation layer with published pricing; Clonable positions as a full continuously-synced clone — both are subscription localization, and both need a human spot-check on quality

tools.name: Close
tools.what_it_does: A high-performance sales CRM built for growth-focused startups and SMBs. Unifies calling, emailing, and SMS into one powerful inbox. Now ships with Chloe, a built-in AI teammate for notetaking, chat, pipeline suggestions and CRM enrichment, with outbound AI voice calling still in beta.
tools.pricing: Per-seat: Solo about $9, Essentials $35, Growth $99, Scale $139 per user/mo billed annually (higher monthly) (2026). Call minutes, SMS and Power Dialer credits are billed separately and can meaningfully raise the real cost.
tools.honest_knock: The built-in calling is the draw, but call and SMS credits stack on top of the seat price — a '$99' plan can effectively cost ~$160/user once a rep dials 50+ times a day. Great for call-heavy teams, pricey if you barely dial.
tools.best_for: inside-sales teams that live on the phone and want calling, SMS and CRM in one place
tools.skip_if: your sales are mostly email or self-serve — a cheaper CRM without built-in calling covers you

tools.name: CloudTalk
tools.what_it_does: Next-generation cloud calling system designed for modern support and sales teams. Includes smart routing and CRM integrations. Its AI voice agents answer inbound calls around the clock, route them or take a message and hand the call to a human; calendar sync with automated booking and rescheduling sits on the paid AI Specialist tier, while the entry-level AI Receptionist still lists appointment scheduling as coming soon.
tools.pricing: Lite €19, Starter €25, Essential €29 and Expert €49 per user/mo on annual billing, and Expert needs at least 3 licences. AI voice agents are separate subscriptions: AI Receptionist from €99/mo with 200 minutes, AI Specialist €349/mo with 1,000 minutes, and above 10,000 minutes a month custom pricing CloudTalk advertises as low as €0.15 per minute. Conversation Intelligence renews at €9 per agent/mo and the Power Dialer is a €15 per user/mo add-on below Expert (re-verified 1 Aug 2026).
tools.honest_knock: The per-seat price is only part of it — number rental, outbound minutes and the AI add-ons stack on top, so a call-heavy team's real bill runs above the plan rate. Solid CRM integrations, but model your call volume first.
tools.best_for: support and sales teams that want a cloud call center with strong CRM integrations and call analytics
tools.skip_if: you make only occasional calls — a basic VoIP line or your CRM's built-in dialer costs far less

tools.name: Cloudways
tools.what_it_does: Managed-hosting layer that rents you servers on DigitalOcean, Vultr, Linode, AWS or Google Cloud through one dashboard, with the stack, caching, staging, cloning, backups and 24/7 platform support pre-built on top. You buy a server and put as many sites on it as it holds — no per-site plans and no visit metering — billed hourly and invoiced monthly in arrears with no contract. The trade is control: Cloudways' own documentation states there is no root access and no bring-your-own cloud account, so the server lives in Cloudways' name. Owned by DigitalOcean since September 2022.
tools.pricing: (read 21 Jul 2026) No free tier, but a 3-day free trial with no credit card required (Cloudways documentation). Billing is hourly and post-paid, invoiced in the first week of the following month, with no annual contract. The entry plan on DigitalOcean is Micro — 2GB RAM, 1 vCPU, 50GB storage, 2TB bandwidth — at $11/month. Further up, the DigitalOcean 8GB/4 vCPU/160GB/5TB plan lists at $88/month, against $48/month for the identical droplet bought direct from DigitalOcean on the same day. Add-ons are monthly and separate: Cloudflare Enterprise CDN from $4.99 per domain, Site Manager from $3 per app, Malware Protection from $4 per app, Rackspace email $1 per mailbox, offsite backup storage $0.033 per GB. Advanced Support is $100/month or 10% of your invoice, whichever is higher, on a six-month minimum; Premium Support is $500/month or 10% on the same terms (a discounted promotion was running when we checked — promotions move, so read the live price). Cloudways Autonomous is a separate autoscaling product at $99, $199 and $399/month. Markups on AWS and Google Cloud cannot be calculated because Cloudways does not publish the underlying instance types. US list prices, excluding tax.
tools.honest_knock: "Fully managed" here means the server, not your site — and that distinction is where the money is. Cloudways' own support page puts infrastructure and platform work in the included tier but treats application help as guidance only: plugin and theme troubleshooting, database work and performance tuning sit behind Advanced Support at $100/month or 10% of your invoice, whichever is higher, on a six-month minimum. On a small server that add-on costs more than the server it supports. Content changes, custom code debugging and code audits stay out of scope on every tier, paid ones included. The deeper catch is ownership: Cloudways documents that you get no root access and cannot use your own cloud credentials, so the machine sits in Cloudways' account — you cannot fire the management layer and keep the server, you migrate. And read the billing terms before you rely on it: their help centre states that an unpaid invoice restricts server access and can lead to the server and its backups being deleted, with backups kept for only 14 days after deletion.
tools.best_for: agencies and PHP shops running many sites who want servers managed but not metered — one server holds as many sites as it can carry with no visit caps, billing is hourly and post-paid with no annual term, and Magento and Laravel are first-class alongside WordPress, so it suits teams who genuinely do not want anyone patching kernels at 2am
tools.skip_if: you are comfortable in a terminal, or you run a single small site — going direct to the cloud provider with your own control panel keeps the server in your own account for materially less, and one low-traffic site is better served by shared hosting or by a per-site managed host that bundles CDN and application support. Cloudways also has no email hosting of its own, reselling a Rackspace add-on instead
compare_with: Going direct on DigitalOcean with your own control panel

DigitalOcean owns Cloudways and sells both sides, which makes this the honest comparison: the same 8GB machine is $48/month as a droplet and $88/month wrapped in Cloudways. Add DigitalOcean's own daily backups and a control-panel licence and a like-for-like self-managed box lands nearer $75-80, so the real premium is smaller than the sticker gap suggests. The decisive difference is not price but ownership: with your own droplet the account and root are yours and you can drop the panel and keep the server, whereas leaving Cloudways is a migration

tools.name: Clutch
tools.what_it_does: B2B services marketplace — submit a free project brief and get matched with verified, best-fit agencies for your project, no research required.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free for buyers: submitting a project brief costs nothing and carries no obligation to hire. Clutch is a B2B services marketplace — you describe a project and get matched with about five verified, best-fit agencies. Agencies invest to be listed and matched; the buyer pays nothing.
tools.honest_knock: It's genuinely free to submit a brief — but be clear on what it is: a lead-generation marketplace, not a neutral directory. Your brief goes straight to agencies who will reach out to pitch you, and providers pay to be visible and matched. It's a fast way to shortlist vetted agencies; just expect the outreach that comes with it.
tools.best_for: businesses that want to skip manual agency research and get matched quickly with vetted, best-fit service providers for a specific project
tools.skip_if: you already have trusted agency relationships, or you'd rather research independently without agencies contacting you
compare_with: G2 and traditional directories make you scroll and compare yourself; Clutch's brief-matching narrows it to a handful of vetted providers fast — the trade-off is that it's a matching marketplace where you'll field agency outreach

tools.name: Cognism
tools.what_it_does: B2B contact data with a GDPR focus — phone-verified mobile numbers and intent signals.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown. Two named plans, Standard and Pro, both stated to include 5 seats, with everything routed to 'Talk to sales' and 'Get a personalised quote'. The model is credit-based — their own wording is that 1 credit equals 1 revealed contact — with credits included in the subscription per seat, but no allowance is published. CRM Enrichment is sold standalone or as an add-on; Data-as-a-Service is priced by volume and delivery method.
tools.honest_knock: No price, no credit allowance, and a five-seat minimum on both named plans. That combination means the smallest deal is five seats of something you cannot price, so budget conversations start with a sales call rather than a number. The credit model is the part to nail down: one credit reveals one contact, so your real cost per usable lead is the credit price divided by your connect rate, and neither figure is published. Before the call, work out how many contacts a month you actually reveal — that is the only number that lets you judge the quote you get, and it is worth asking whether unused credits roll over, because nothing on the page says.
tools.best_for: outbound sales teams in Europe who need mobile numbers that are actually verified and care about GDPR provenance — that is the specific thing this is better at
tools.skip_if: you are one or two people prospecting, because both named plans include five seats; also skip it if your market is US-only, where the data advantage is smaller and cheaper options exist
compare_with: the standing comparison in B2B data — Apollo publishes its prices, which makes it the honest starting benchmark for whatever Cognism quotes you

tools.name: CometChat
tools.what_it_does: In-app text, voice and video chat infrastructure to embed into your own software — secure and scalable, with a free developer plan and, via the new Air release, fully on-prem or air-gapped deployment for regulated enterprises.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free Build tier for development ($0/mo, all features, up to 100 users). Paid tiers are now published: Basic $239/mo and Advanced $359/mo, both billed annually (paying monthly costs ~20% more). Above Advanced, Enterprise is custom, starting from 10k MAU. Overages stack on top: $0.10 per MAU and $1 per concurrent connection beyond the 5%-of-MAU included allotment; messages and storage are unlimited, with 6-month message retention. (re-verified 18 Jul 2026)
tools.honest_knock: The pricing cliff is the honest headline: from a 100-MAU free tier straight to ~$239/mo is a brutal jump for an early-stage app, and users report plan structures changing under them — so model your MAU growth curve and the overage math before you architect around it. Chat infrastructure is sticky by nature; the time to compare vendors is before launch, not after.
tools.best_for: product teams that want proven in-app text/voice/video chat with SDKs for every major framework, without building messaging infrastructure themselves
tools.skip_if: your app is pre-revenue with growing users (the free-to-paid cliff will hit mid-growth), or chat is peripheral enough that a support widget covers it
compare_with: the premium chat-SDK peers — all three are MAU-priced; compare at YOUR projected MAU including overages, not at the entry tier

tools.name: Compliancely
tools.what_it_does: Compliance and verification API for US businesses and individuals: real-time and bulk IRS TIN matching, KYB business verification, USPS address and Secretary of State lookups, Form I-9 and E-Verify, consent-based IRS tax transcript retrieval, and ongoing OFAC, watchlist and FATCA monitoring. Built by Zenwork, the company behind Tax1099.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-29, re-verified 2026-08-05, read in a live browser session on their own pricing page, both billing toggles) The published price list covers one product only: TIN-match volume. Billed annually, Essential 25 is $16.95/mo for 25 monthly TIN verifications ($0.67 per match), Essential 50 $32.54/mo ($0.65), Essential 75 $45.79/mo ($0.61), Plus 100 $57.99/mo ($0.57) and Plus 250 $135.04/mo ($0.54). Switch the toggle to monthly billing and the same five tiers read $19.95, $38.49, $53.95, $67.95 and $159.95 per month, at $0.79 down to $0.63 per match — the page advertises 15% off for annual billing, and the real gap holds at roughly 15% on every tier. Enterprise is quote-only. Everything else Compliancely sells carries no public price at all: the business verification and credit-risk report packages, address verification, Form I-9, IRS tax transcripts and income verification each end in Contact Sales or Book a Demo rather than a number. Compliancely's partner team told us on 5 August 2026 that the published tiers are meant for buyers up to roughly 3,000 checks and that anything above that moves to a custom quote — that threshold is theirs, not a number the pricing page states.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing page prices one product and the marketing sells about a dozen. Every tier you can actually buy online is an allowance of TIN verifications; the moment you want the things the homepage leads with — KYB business verification, credit-risk assessment, address verification, Form I-9 and E-Verify, IRS tax transcripts, OFAC and watchlist monitoring — the button changes from Get Started to Contact Sales. So the compliance stack this tool is pitched as has no advertised cost, and the number you can see is the smallest part of it. The second thing to read carefully is that the tiers are allowances rather than rates. You commit to a monthly verification count up front, and the per-match price moves against the smallest buyers: $0.79 a check on the cheapest month-to-month plan versus $0.54 on the largest annual one, a 46% spread that falls the wrong way for anyone testing the product at low volume. If your usage is lumpy — a filing-season spike and eleven quiet months — an allowance you buy every month is the wrong shape, and the prepaid option the page offers as a third toggle is worth asking about before you subscribe.
tools.best_for: finance, tax and HR teams with a steady monthly volume of US identity and business checks, who would rather buy TIN matching, KYB, I-9 and sanctions screening behind one API than integrate three separate vendors — and who are willing to run a sales conversation to price the modules beyond TIN matching
tools.skip_if: you need a handful of one-off verifications a year, because the cheapest plan still bills a monthly allowance whether you use it or not and the per-match rate is at its worst down there; or you need the full cost of a compliance stack on paper before you talk to a salesperson, since only the TIN-match tiers are published
compare_with: the honest head-to-head is Checkr, which owns one slice of what Compliancely does — employment and identity screening — and owns it with the more mature product and public self-serve pricing. If background checks are the job, Checkr wins; Compliancely is the broader bet when IRS TIN matching and KYB sit at the centre of the workflow rather than hiring. Tax1099 belongs in the conversation for an odder reason: it is family. Zenwork, Inc. is named in Compliancely's own footer and builds Tax1099 too, so the filing product and the verification product come out of one house — complements rather than rivals, and worth raising as an integration question before you price either. Verify both current price lists yourself; ours were read on 2026-07-29.

tools.name: Connecteam
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one app for managing deskless teams. Scheduling, time clock, tasks, training and team chat for hourly and frontline workforces.
tools.pricing: Genuinely free for small businesses up to 10 users (all features, no time limit); paid hubs (Operations, Communications, HR) each start around $35/mo for up to 30 users and scale to about $119/mo, with annual billing roughly 18% cheaper (2026).
tools.honest_knock: The free-for-10 plan is one of the most generous in the category, but the three-hub structure means costs can stack if you need all of them — price the specific hubs you'll actually use, not the full bundle.
tools.best_for: deskless and frontline teams (shift work, field crews) that need scheduling, a time clock and comms in one app, on the free-for-10 plan
tools.skip_if: your whole team sits at desks with email and Slack — this is built for the frontline, and a general PM tool fits an office better

tools.name: Consensus
tools.what_it_does: An AI search engine trained purely on peer-reviewed scientific research. The ultimate tool to avoid AI hallucinations.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free tier with essential search; Pro about $15/mo (or ~$10/mo billed annually) with unlimited Pro searches and 15 Deep searches; a Deep tier adds ~200 Deep searches for power users; Teams/Enterprise custom.
tools.honest_knock: It searches peer-reviewed literature, which is its strength and its boundary: it can tell you what published studies found, not whether those studies are good — study quality, sample sizes and conflicting results still need your judgment, and the AI summary layer can smooth over genuine scientific disagreement. Treat it as a dramatically faster literature scan, not an oracle; click through to the papers that matter.
tools.best_for: researchers, clinicians, students and writers who want evidence-backed answers drawn from peer-reviewed papers instead of the open web
tools.skip_if: your questions are practical/commercial rather than research-based (a general AI assistant fits), or you need full systematic-review rigor (this accelerates it, not replaces it)
compare_with: the research-AI peer set — Consensus leans consumer-friendly consensus summaries; Elicit leans structured extraction for reviews

tools.name: Contractor Foreman
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one construction management software. Handle estimating, scheduling, daily logs, and financial tracking effortlessly from the job site.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Priced for the company rather than per seat, with unlimited projects on every tier. Annual: Basic $49/month ($588 a year, 1 user), Standard $105 ($1,264, 3 users), Plus $166 ($1,997, 8 users), Pro $221 ($2,654, 15 users), Unlimited $332 ($3,984, unlimited users). Quarterly costs more for the same plans: Standard $132/month, Plus $206, Pro $282, Unlimited $415. Basic is not offered quarterly. Their own wording: the fee listed is the fee for the company as a whole.
tools.honest_knock: Credit where it is due first: this is company pricing with unlimited projects and no per-user overage inside your tier, which is rare in construction software and genuinely cheaper than per-seat rivals for a crew. The catch is the billing term. Quarterly costs 26% more than annual on the same plan — $132 against $105 on Standard — and Basic is not sold quarterly at all, so the cheapest way in requires a year paid up front. The user counts are the real ladder: 1, 3, 8, 15, unlimited. A five-person crew is not on Standard at $105, it is on Plus at $166, so count your licence holders before you compare against anything else.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size contractors who want estimating, scheduling and daily logs in one place and can commit to a year — the company-wide fee makes it cheap per head once you have a crew
tools.skip_if: you are a sole trader with a handful of jobs, because Basic at $49 a month annual is real money against a spreadsheet and a calendar; also skip it if you need to try before committing, since annual is where the price works
compare_with: the standing comparison in construction software — compare total company cost at your crew size, since the per-seat rivals overtake this quickly

tools.name: Convert
tools.what_it_does: Privacy-first A/B testing platform — experiments, personalization and feature rollouts, priced by tested users. Via our link: an exclusive 30-day full-access trial (standard is 15 days).
tools.pricing: (2026) 15-day standard free trial — through our link it's an exclusive 30-day full-access trial (verified 16 Jul 2026, no credit card). Growth $399/mo, or $299/mo paid annually ($3,588/yr), for 100K tested users a month; Pro $599/mo, or $420/mo annually ($5,040/yr); Enterprise on request. Overuse is metered — $399 per extra 100K on Growth, $699 per 250K on Pro (it can be switched off) — and each additional custom domain costs $1,000/year.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is tested users, and it keeps running: blow past your monthly allowance and overuse blocks land at $399-699 unless you hard-cap them — and every extra custom domain is $1,000 a year. The friendly $299 headline assumes annual prepay; month-to-month is $399.
tools.best_for: CRO teams running serious A/B and multivariate testing who want a privacy-first, GDPR-friendly alternative to the big experimentation suites
tools.skip_if: your traffic is modest — statistical significance needs volume, and 100K tested users a month is more than most small sites can use — or your landing-page tool's built-in testing covers it
compare_with: VWO is the broad experimentation suite where testing is one module; Convert focuses squarely on A/B testing with GDPR-first positioning — compare the add-on costs (API, domains) on both before deciding

tools.name: CrankWheel
tools.what_it_does: Instant, no-download screen sharing built for sales calls. Share your screen with a prospect in seconds from any device to close deals faster.
tools.pricing: (2026) A free plan (1 user, 15 meetings/mo), Solo about $29/user/mo (unlimited screen sharing, ~48% off on annual), Team about $89–$99/mo with shared meeting pools; Enterprise custom. Free trial available.
tools.honest_knock: It's deliberately narrow — instant, no-download screen sharing for sales calls — so it's excellent at that one job and thin everywhere else: no full video-conferencing suite, no deep collaboration or webinar tooling. The free and Solo tiers cap meetings, which an active rep will hit. If you want an all-purpose meeting platform, this isn't it; if you want prospects to see your screen in seconds with zero friction, that focus is exactly why it works.
tools.best_for: sales reps, insurance agents and consultants who need prospects to view a screen instantly with no download or install, on any device
tools.skip_if: you need full video conferencing, webinars or team collaboration (Zoom/Meet fit better), or your call volume stays under the free tier
compare_with: general meeting platforms — CrankWheel's edge is zero-friction, no-download instant sharing for live sales, not full conferencing

tools.name: Crazy Egg
tools.what_it_does: Website optimization with heatmaps, scroll maps, session recordings and A/B testing — see how visitors behave and lift conversions with data.
tools.pricing: From $29/mo to $499, billed annually only (no real monthly option); it bills per pageview, so your bill swings with pages-per-session (2026).
tools.honest_knock: The entry plan is thin on recordings (~100/mo vs Hotjar's free ~1,050), heatmaps need manual per-page and per-device setup, and annual-only billing locks you in. Like all these tools it's diagnostic — it shows what's broken, it doesn't fix it.
tools.best_for: lean marketing teams that want heatmaps and built-in A/B testing in one affordable, consolidated tool
tools.skip_if: you want generous recordings, automatic heatmaps and qualitative feedback — Hotjar's free tier and product depth suit product teams better

tools.name: Credit Repair Cloud
tools.what_it_does: The leading software to start, run, and grow a highly profitable credit repair business from anywhere in the world.
tools.pricing: (2026) Five plans from Personal about $49/mo up to Enterprise about $599/mo (Start ~$179, Grow ~$299, Scale ~$399), scaling by active clients and team seats; roughly 20% off annual, 30-day trial, no contract.
tools.honest_knock: This is business-in-a-box software for starting a credit-repair company, not a tool that repairs your own credit — the price only makes sense if you're actually building a client business on it. The middle tiers jump fast as you add clients and seats, and success depends far more on your sales and compliance discipline (credit repair is a regulated space) than on the software. Buy it as an operator, not a consumer.
tools.best_for: entrepreneurs building or running a credit-repair business who need client management, dispute automation and done-for-you letter workflows
tools.skip_if: you just want to fix your own personal credit (you don't need this), or you're not prepared for the sales and compliance work a client business demands
compare_with: Dispute Fox or Client Dispute Manager
comparable credit-repair business platforms — compare on client limits and automation depth at your stage

tools.name: CrowdStrike
tools.what_it_does: Endpoint protection built around a cloud-delivered agent: antivirus, EDR and threat hunting.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Priced per device. Falcon Go $7.99 per device per month, or $59.99 per device billed annually — capped at a maximum of 100 devices. Falcon Pro $14.99 monthly or $99.99 annually per device. Falcon Enterprise $19.99 per device per month. Larger tiers and managed services are quote-only. A free trial is offered on every tier.
tools.honest_knock: Two numbers decide whether this is for you, and neither is the headline. The first is the 100-device ceiling on Falcon Go: it is not a soft limit you grow through, it is the point where you change product. The second is the annual rate, which is worth doing the division on — $59.99 a year against $7.99 a month is $95.88, so annual saves 37%, one of the larger annual discounts in security software. Beyond that, be honest with yourself about which tier you are comparing: Go is antivirus with a good agent, and the endpoint detection and response that CrowdStrike is famous for starts at Pro. Comparing Go against a full EDR product from a competitor is comparing the wrong things.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size companies that want a serious endpoint agent without running a security team — Falcon Go is genuinely priced for businesses under 100 devices
tools.skip_if: you are under ten devices and already run a maintained operating system with its built-in protection, because at that size the management overhead outweighs the gain; also skip Go if you actually need EDR, since that starts a tier up
compare_with: SentinelOne or Microsoft Defender for Business
the direct endpoint peers — Defender is often already in your Microsoft licence, so price that first before comparing per-device rates

tools.name: Customer.io
tools.what_it_does: Behavioural messaging: email, push and in-app campaigns driven by product events rather than lists.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Essentials starts at $100 a month billed monthly, scaled by profiles. Premium starts at $1,000 a month billed yearly. Enterprise is quote-only. Overages are published, which is unusual and useful: additional people and object profiles $0.009 each on Essentials, additional 1,000 emails $0.12, additional AI credits $10 per 100,000. Essentials includes 2 workspaces; Premium and Enterprise unlimited. Early-stage companies that have raised under $10M can get twelve months free through their startup programme.
tools.honest_knock: The gap between the two published tiers is the thing to plan around: $100 to $1,000 a month is ten times, and there is nothing in between. What pushes you across is not a feature you choose but your profile count growing, so the honest question at signup is what your list looks like in a year rather than today. Credit where due — the overage rates are printed, at $0.009 a profile and $0.12 per thousand emails, which most tools in this category will not tell you until the invoice. Use those numbers: growing into overage on Essentials is often cheaper than the jump to Premium, and you can work out exactly where the crossover is.
tools.best_for: product-led companies whose messaging is triggered by what people do in the product rather than by a list — that is what this is built for and it is genuinely better at it than list-first tools
tools.skip_if: you send newsletters and campaigns to a list — that is a different job and much cheaper elsewhere; also skip it if your profile count is unpredictable, since profiles are the meter
compare_with: the direct behavioural-messaging peers — Klaviyo for ecommerce, Braze at enterprise scale; compare on cost per profile at your projected list size

tools.name: Databox
tools.what_it_does: Centralized KPI dashboards. Pull data from all your software tools into one clean interface to monitor your business health. A free Skills Marketplace adds guided analyses on top: the paid-ads skill standardizes every ad channel into one efficiency table with CPA gauges against your own targets, judged per funnel role. A native MCP server (mcp.databox.com) puts those metrics inside ChatGPT or Claude — ingest data and query it in plain language. It runs on every paid plan, not on Free, and its queries spend from the same monthly AI-credit pool as Genie.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-07-29) There is a free plan: Free at $0 with 3 data sources, 1 user, 1 dashboard or report and 50 AI credits a month. Paid tiers, billed annually: Analyst $64/mo (5 data sources, 1 user, 500 AI credits), Pro $159/mo (3 sources included, $5.60/mo per extra, unlimited users, 1,500 credits), Growth $399/mo (4,000 credits, 15-minute sync) and a custom tier. AI credits are one shared monthly pool for the Genie assistant and the MCP server, so heavy AI use is what moves you up a tier rather than seats.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing model bites: Pro connects only 3 data sources, so the per-source fees stack up fast — and for agencies juggling many clients with diverse tools it gets expensive. Power users may also find the custom-metric and data-modelling depth limited next to a full BI tool.
tools.best_for: SMBs and agencies that want clean KPI dashboards from 130+ one-click integrations without building them by hand
tools.skip_if: you only need one or two data sources (the per-source fees add up), or you want deep custom data modelling — a free tool like Looker Studio fits better

tools.name: Deel
tools.what_it_does: Global hiring, payroll and EOR platform — pay contractors and employees compliantly in 150+ countries, from $49 per contractor per month, with HR tools and US PEO options.
tools.pricing: (2026) Per-worker pricing, demo-led: HR/hiring tools from $14 per worker/month; Contractors from $49 per contractor/month, or $325/month per Contractor of Record; US PEO from $125 per employee/month; EOR (Deel employs your international hire for you) from $599 per employee/month. Free demo; final quotes come through sales.
tools.honest_knock: Every price is a ‘starting at’ and every button says ‘book a demo’ — the real bill depends on countries, benefits and add-ons, and only firms up in a sales conversation. And know what EOR money buys: at $599+/month per employee you’re paying for compliance risk transfer, not software — worth it in unfamiliar jurisdictions, expensive where you could open your own entity.
tools.best_for: companies hiring internationally without local entities — contractors paid compliantly in 150+ countries, or full EOR employment where you need someone on the ground fast
tools.skip_if: your team is all-domestic (a local payroll tool is far cheaper), or you hire enough people in one country that opening your own entity beats paying per-employee EOR fees forever
compare_with: Gusto is the friendly US-payroll incumbent for domestic teams; Deel is built for global — contractors, EOR and payroll across 150+ countries. Pick by where your people are

tools.name: Deputy
tools.what_it_does: Workforce management for hourly and shift-based teams: rota building, time clocking, timesheet approval and labour-law compliance, with payroll and HR integrations.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-31, read in a live browser session on deputy.com/pricing with both billing toggles) Three plans, per user per month and excluding tax. On annual billing Lite is $5, Core $6.50 and Pro $9; switch the toggle to monthly and the same three read $5.50, $7.25 and $10. Add-ons are billed monthly on top: HR $2 per user, Messaging+ $1.95 per user and Analytics+ $1.50 per user (the last two are included in Pro), plus Deputy Payroll enabled by Paycor at $8 per user plus a $49 monthly base fee, which is only available on annual Core and Pro plans in the US. The page also states a minimum monthly spend of USD $30 / AUD $30 / GBP £20 per invoice on the monthly Lite, Core and Pro plans. Lite and Core start with a free trial; Pro is Contact us rather than self-serve.
tools.honest_knock: The minimum monthly spend is the number to check before anything else: at $5.50 per user on monthly billing, a team of fewer than about six people still pays the $30 floor, so the headline per-user price is misleading at small scale. Beyond that, the plan you probably want is not the one you first price — auto-scheduling, demand forecasting and labour budgets sit in Core, and SSO, custom access levels and location hierarchies only in Pro, which has no public self-serve checkout. The add-ons stack per user as well, and the payroll add-on is US-only and annual-only.
tools.best_for: shift-based businesses — hospitality, retail, healthcare, any hourly workforce — that need rostering, clocking and labour-law compliance in one system and have enough staff to clear the minimum spend
tools.skip_if: you run a small salaried desk team: the $30 monthly minimum means you pay for roughly six users whether you have them or not, and salaried staff rarely need shift-level clocking at all

tools.name: Descript
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered video and podcast editor: edit media by editing the text transcript — cut, overdub and remove filler words like editing a doc — with screen recording, AI voice cloning and an AI assistant (Underlord) built in.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free plan (60 min/mo, watermarked 720p exports); Hobbyist about $24/mo, Creator $35, Business $65 per editor — roughly a third cheaper billed annually ($16/$24/$50). Media hours and AI credits are capped per tier (10/30/40 hrs, 400-1,500 credits/mo).
tools.honest_knock: It's per-editor pricing with two meters running underneath: media hours AND monthly AI credits. Heavy podcast or video volume burns through the caps fast, and the free tier watermarks 720p exports — model your real production hours before picking a tier.
tools.best_for: podcasters and video creators who want to edit by editing the transcript — cutting, overdubbing and stripping filler words as easily as editing a doc
tools.skip_if: you need frame-precise, effects-heavy editing (a traditional NLE fits better) or your monthly volume blows past the media-hour caps
compare_with: Riverside wins on recording-quality-first workflows, CapCut on quick social edits; Descript wins on the text-based editing workflow itself

tools.name: Devs.ai
tools.what_it_does: Build AI apps and agents without heavy engineering. Combine multiple leading LLMs to create chatbots and internal tools your team can actually use.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-05, read in a live browser session on devs.ai/home/pricing with both billing toggles) Devs.ai does publish its pricing — on the marketing site at devs.ai/home/pricing, not at the app's /pricing route, which bounces you to a login screen. Free is $0 forever, but Agent Builder and App Builder appear there in "Core" rather than "Full" form, data upload is capped at 2 GB, and workflows, APIs and integrations are marked absent. Personal is $15 per seat / month billed annually or $18 billed monthly; Business is $30 per seat / month annually or $36 monthly; Enterprise is a custom annual contract. The seat fee is not the whole bill: Personal includes $10 of usage per month and Business $21, with model usage metered on top of the seat. Data upload runs 2 GB, 10 GB, 20 GB and custom across the four tiers. Team governance and collaboration start at Business, while SSO (OpenID/SAML), access control lists, custom connectors and white-labelling are Enterprise-only. Separately, Devs.ai told us by email on 5 August 2026 that organisations upgrading to a paid Personal or Business plan can earn up to $100 in usage credits for completing setup steps — starting a conversation, creating an agent, connecting an integration, deploying an app — that the credits are shared org-wide and do not expire, and that Enterprise is excluded while orgs already on a paid plan before July 2026 are not enrolled by default. That last paragraph is the vendor's own statement to us, not something we found published on the pricing page.
tools.honest_knock: The seat price is the smaller half of the bill. Personal includes $10 of usage a month and Business $21, with model usage metered on top of the seat — and the plan cards state the included amount without stating the rate you pay once it runs out, which is exactly the number you need to forecast a real workload. The free plan is a demo rather than a working tier: both builders are limited to "Core", and workflows, APIs and integrations are absent entirely, which is much of what would make the platform useful past a first agent. And for a product sold on IT governance, the governance controls are the ones you cannot buy with a card — SSO, access control lists and white-labelling sit on the Enterprise tier, behind a custom annual contract.
tools.best_for: teams that want to prototype and ship AI agents and apps across multiple models without engineering overhead, and that can absorb model usage metered on top of the per-seat fee
tools.skip_if: you need SSO, access control lists or white-labelling without going through an Enterprise contract, or you need one predictable all-in bill rather than a seat fee plus metered usage
compare_with: the agent-builder field — all three meter model usage differently on top of their base price, so compare on the metered layer rather than on the seat fee

tools.name: Dext
tools.what_it_does: Bookkeeping automation: capture receipts and invoices, extract the data automatically and sync to your accounting software — less manual entry.
tools.pricing: From ~£24/mo (Starter) to £42 (Growing) and £84 (Business) — roughly $31–239 depending on plan and region (2026).
tools.honest_knock: It's a data-capture layer, not accounting software — it feeds Xero, QuickBooks or Sage, so you still need one of those. Extraction accuracy varies and sometimes needs manual fixes, the UI is tricky for beginners, the mobile app is more limited than desktop, and sole traders find it pricey.
tools.best_for: accountants, bookkeepers and growing businesses drowning in receipts who want fast, accurate capture flowing straight into Xero, QuickBooks or Sage
tools.skip_if: you're a sole trader with few receipts (pricey for low volume), or you want all-in-one accounting — Dext only does the capture layer
compare_with: the free-with-Xero and the do-it-yourself routes

tools.name: Dify
tools.what_it_does: Leading open-source platform for building agentic AI workflows and LLM apps. Visual builder, RAG pipelines and model-agnostic — ship AI features without reinventing the plumbing.
tools.pricing: Genuinely open-source and free to self-host (you pay only infrastructure plus your own LLM API bills); the managed cloud adds a free Sandbox, Professional about $59/mo and Team around $159/mo (2026). LLM inference always bills separately from your provider.
tools.honest_knock: 'Free' self-hosting isn't free — you own the servers, updates and reliability, and LLM tokens cost extra on every plan. It's powerful, but you need some technical comfort to run and maintain it well.
tools.best_for: technical teams that want to build and ship LLM apps and agents on an open-source platform they can self-host and control
tools.skip_if: you want a no-maintenance, non-technical builder — a fully managed no-code AI tool saves you the infra and upkeep
compare_with: Flowise or a managed platform like Lindy.ai
other LLM-app builders, self-host or managed

tools.name: Diginius
tools.what_it_does: Digital marketing and e-commerce performance platform. Manage PPC, analytics and product feeds to improve online sales and visibility.
tools.pricing: (2026) Essential about $20/mo (single user); Pro ~$99/mo (5 users); Core ~$249/mo (10 users, most features); Business/custom above. ~20% off annual; 14-day trial.
tools.honest_knock: All-in-one marketing dashboards live or die on data depth per module: Diginius bundles PPC, SEO, lead intelligence and reporting affordably, but specialists (a dedicated SEO suite, a dedicated PPC optimizer) go deeper in their lanes — so buy it as consolidation for a lean team, not as a replacement for expert-grade tooling in your primary channel. Verify the integrations you depend on (especially Microsoft Ads, its historical strength) in the trial.
tools.best_for: lean teams and agencies that want PPC, SEO and lead intelligence consolidated in one affordable dashboard instead of five subscriptions
tools.skip_if: your growth lives in one channel where a specialist tool's depth pays for itself, or you need enterprise analytics rigor
compare_with: the specialist suites — deeper per channel at higher cost; Diginius wins on breadth-per-dollar for generalists

tools.name: doola
tools.what_it_does: Business formation and compliance made easy. Launch your US LLC or C-Corp from anywhere globally, complete with banking and tax management.
tools.pricing: Starter about $297/yr (LLC or C-Corp formation, EIN, registered agent, US address); Pulse bookkeeping ~$300/yr; Tax and Compliance ~$1,999/yr; Business-in-a-Box ~$2,999/yr — plus state filing fees on top ($50-500 by state) (2026).
tools.honest_knock: Formation is the cheap part; the recurring bookkeeping and tax tiers are where the real cost sits, and state fees are extra on top of doola's price. Convenient especially for non-US founders, but a local accountant may be cheaper once you're established.
tools.best_for: founders (often non-US) who want US LLC/C-Corp formation, EIN and compliance handled in one place without the paperwork
tools.skip_if: you're a US resident comfortable filing formation yourself — the state fee plus a cheap registered agent costs far less than the bundle
compare_with: other formation services, or doing it yourself

tools.name: Dripify
tools.what_it_does: Cloud-based LinkedIn outreach automation — drip sequences of connection requests, messages, InMails and profile views, with configurable daily limits and a built-in email finder. From $39 per user/month billed annually, 7-day free trial without a card.
tools.pricing: (2026-07-24, read on their own pricing page) Four tiers, priced per user: Basic $39, Pro $59 and Advanced $79 per user per month billed annually, plus an Enterprise tier that is quote-only. A 7-day free trial runs without a credit card. Those are the annual-billing rates. Month to month the same tiers read $59, $79 and $99 per user (both columns read in a live browser session on 2026-07-24), so the 'up to 35% off' the toggle advertises is real but front-loaded — you pay a year up front to get it, and the discount shrinks as you go up the range: about 34 percent on Basic, 25 on Pro, 20 on Advanced. What each tier buys is unusually consequential here: Basic gets you one drip campaign and what the page calls 'limited daily quotas'; unlimited campaigns and full quotas start at Pro; Advanced adds multi-team management and the safety feature Dripify itself recommends. Every tier includes 100 email-finder credits a month.
tools.honest_knock: Understand what you are buying before the price matters: LinkedIn prohibits this entire product category. Its User Agreement bans using 'bots or other unauthorized automated methods' to 'send or redirect messages', and its prohibited-software page says members using such tools 'risk having their accounts restricted or shut down'. There is no carve-out for cloud tools or low volumes, and Dripify is not an outlier here — every competitor sits on the same side of that line. Dripify's own documentation is candid about the consequence, warning that LinkedIn 'may issue warnings, temporary restrictions, or even permanent bans', and it publishes a recovery procedure for exactly that scenario. Two things follow. First, the advertised ceiling is not a working speed: the app allows up to 75 connection requests a day, while Dripify's own setup guide tells beginners to run 10 to 15, and brand-new accounts 2 to 5, building up 10 to 20 percent a week. Anyone buying on the headline number is buying capacity they are told not to use. Second, Activity Control — the feature Dripify names as its best protection, which adjusts your pace automatically — sits on the $79 Advanced tier. On Basic and Pro, safe pacing is your own manual responsibility. And when a vendor writes that a feature 'makes sure your LinkedIn account won't get flagged', read that as a claim about a third party's enforcement decisions that no vendor can actually guarantee.
tools.best_for: sales teams that already run LinkedIn outreach, understand that automation breaches LinkedIn's terms, and accept that risk with their eyes open — the cloud architecture means sequences run with your browser closed and no extension injected into your session
tools.skip_if: anyone whose LinkedIn account is not expendable, since a restriction can be permanent and no tool can promise otherwise; or anyone tempted by the 75-a-day ceiling, because the vendor's own advice is roughly a fifth of that
compare_with: the closest head-to-head — both are cloud-based with a regional dedicated IP, so the 'cloud versus extension' framing you will read in affiliate roundups does not actually separate them. The real difference is the pricing model: Expandi sells one Business plan with everything included at $99 per user a month, 20 percent off annually, while Dripify tiers both quotas and safety features. Watch the $39-versus-$99 gap that roundups quote — that is Dripify's annual rate against Expandi's monthly one. Month against month it is $59 to $99 versus $99, and at the top of Dripify's range the two cost the same. Both price lists read on 2026-07-24; verify them yourself before you buy.

tools.name: DropGenius
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered dropshipping store builder. Launch a ready-to-sell online store with products, branding and copy generated in minutes.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 5 Aug 2026) Monthly: Starter $39, Pro $59, Empire $99, Unicorn $299, each with a 14-day free trial. Switch to annual billing and Starter disappears from the table; the rest become Pro $24/mo (billed annually at $288), Empire $57/mo ($684) and Unicorn $79/mo ($948). Their own FAQ still quotes an older $39.99-$299.99 range plus a $1.99 one-time store-creation fee, so the marketing copy and the checkout do not agree. The store it builds runs on Shopify, which bills you separately — DropGenius does not state that cost anywhere on its pages.
tools.honest_knock: We have to be blunt here: DropGenius carries a very poor Trustpilot rating (around 1.6/5 at research time), with recurring complaints about charges continuing after cancellation and refund difficulty. An AI-generated store in 30 seconds is also just a starting template — the product selection, marketing and margins remain entirely your problem. If you proceed: pay attention to cancellation mechanics from day one, screenshot everything, and treat the Renewal Radar as mandatory equipment.
tools.best_for: absolute beginners who want a pre-built Shopify dropshipping store scaffold in minutes and understand it's a starting point, not a business
tools.skip_if: anyone uncomfortable with the documented billing complaints — or expecting an AI-generated store to sell by itself
compare_with: building on Spocket directly (same ecosystem) gives you the supplier network without the store-generator layer — and cleaner reviews

tools.name: Dryground AI
tools.what_it_does: Full-stack AI implementation services: helps businesses design and integrate AI across their tech stack — for teams that want AI built and shipped, not just advised.
tools.pricing: Custom, quote-based — this is a services engagement, not a self-serve subscription.
tools.honest_knock: This is consulting, not a tool you log into: best when you want AI designed and built for you, not when you'd rather DIY with software.
tools.best_for: businesses that want AI solutions built for them as a services engagement rather than assembling tools themselves
