tools.skip_if: you're looking for self-serve software with published pricing — this is custom, quote-based consulting

tools.name: EasyDMARC
tools.what_it_does: DMARC, SPF and DKIM monitoring — stop others sending email as your domain.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Plus €44.99/month (€35.99/month billed annually), 2 domains, 100,000–1,000,000 messages/month, 3 months of report history, 1 invited user. Premium €89.99/month (€71.99 annually), 4 domains, up to 5,000,000 messages/month, 1 year of history, unlimited users, a customer-success manager on yearly billing only. Enterprise quote-only with unlimited domains and 3 years of history. A free plan exists but the pricing page shows only the €0 without listing what it includes.
tools.honest_knock: You are buying domains and history, not features. Plus covers two domains; a company with a main domain, a marketing subdomain and a legacy domain it forgot about is already over. And the history window is the part that bites later: three months on Plus means that when you are investigating a spoofing campaign that started in the spring, the reports are gone. The page also does not say what happens when you pass the message volume — their own FAQ does, and the answer is that you lose access to your reports and dashboard rather than being billed for overage, which is a harsher failure mode than an overage charge and worth knowing before you size the plan.
tools.best_for: anyone who sends email from their own domain and has not yet got DMARC to enforcement — the reporting is the part that makes that safe rather than guesswork
tools.skip_if: you have one domain, send little email, and are willing to read raw XML reports yourself, because the free tier plus patience covers the same ground
compare_with: the direct DMARC-platform peers — compare on domains included and history retention, not on the feature list

tools.name: eDesk
tools.what_it_does: E-commerce helpdesk: one unified inbox for Amazon, eBay, Shopify and email, with order data and an AI Agent that bills per resolved outcome. Free plan; paid from $39/agent/mo (annual).
tools.pricing: (verified 17 Jul 2026) Free plan to start; Essential $39/agent/mo, Growth $89/agent/mo (Recommended), Professional $119/agent/mo, Enterprise custom — all billed annually (20% off vs monthly). The AI Agent is included on paid tiers but its automated resolutions bill separately at $0.99 per outcome — you only pay when it actually resolves a query, not per attempt.
tools.honest_knock: Two meters, and the second one is easy to miss: the per-agent price is the entry ticket, but the AI Agent charges $0.99 for every automated resolution on top — great when it deflects real tickets, but a variable line item that scales with your support volume, so model it against your ticket count before assuming a flat bill. And the honest fundamental for any e-commerce helpdesk: the value is only as good as your marketplace integrations actually syncing — test Amazon/eBay/Shopify connections with your real accounts during the free trial.
tools.best_for: e-commerce and marketplace sellers who want one unified inbox across Amazon, eBay, Shopify and email — with order data and AI-assisted replies where support and revenue overlap
tools.skip_if: you run a non-commerce SaaS or service business (general helpdesks fit better and cheaper), or your ticket volume is low enough that a shared inbox already copes
compare_with: Gorgias is the other big e-commerce helpdesk, deepest on Shopify; eDesk leans harder into marketplaces (Amazon, eBay) and per-outcome AI pricing — pick by where your orders actually live and how you want the AI billed

tools.name: ElevateForward
tools.what_it_does: An operational execution and alignment platform (Elevate Studio) for scaling companies, structured in three layers — Strategy (set priorities and initiatives), Execution (track initiatives, workstreams, ownership and KPIs), and Momentum (adoption, change management and follow-through). It turns strategy into structured, visible execution rather than task lists.
tools.pricing: Pricing isn't publicly listed — it's scoped through a conversation rather than a sign-up page, so you'll need to talk to them to know what it costs.
tools.honest_knock: It's a strategy-to-execution layer, not a task app or a dashboard — so the value only lands if leadership actually adopts the framework. 'Operational alignment platform' is also a fuzzy, crowded label, so press them on the concrete deliverables (the diagnostics, KPI blueprints and execution plans) before committing.
tools.best_for: scaling companies where growth is outpacing alignment — leadership lacks execution visibility and strategic initiatives keep stalling halfway
tools.skip_if: you already have solid execution discipline, or you just want a simple task or project tool — this is a strategy-and-alignment layer, not a to-do list
compare_with: an EOS/Traction-style operating system plus your existing PM and BI tools
the pieces EF tries to combine into one

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.what_it_does: Market-leading AI voice platform: hyper-realistic text-to-speech, voice cloning, dubbing, sound effects and conversational agents — with a developer API and a free tier to test voices before you pay.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 16 Jul 2026) Free $0 with 10k credits/mo; Starter $6/mo (30k credits, commercial license); Creator $22/mo — first month 50% off at $11 — with ~121k credits; Pro $99/mo (~600k credits, 44.1kHz PCM); Scale $299/mo (~1.8M credits, 3 workspace seats); Business $990/mo adds low-latency TTS. Extra usage runs roughly $0.36 down to $0.17 per additional minute depending on tier.
tools.honest_knock: Credits are the meter and retakes are the tax — regenerate a paragraph three times and you pay three times, so real usage lands well above the calculator estimate. And read the free-tier fine print: $0 gets you 10k credits to play with, but no commercial license — anything you publish commercially needs at least the $6 Starter. Voice realism genuinely leads the market; niche names and jargon can still need manual retakes, so run your hardest paragraph through the free tier before subscribing.
tools.best_for: creators, developers and product teams that want the most realistic AI voices available — voiceovers, audiobooks, dubbing, conversational agents and a well-documented API
tools.skip_if: you generate hours of long-form audio on a tight budget (credit math punishes volume — flat-hour tools or the TTS built into your video editor may be enough), or you need acted emotional range only a human voice actor delivers
compare_with: Murf counters with studio workflow and per-language breadth, Descript bundles voice into a full video/podcast editor — ElevenLabs' edge is raw voice realism and the developer API

tools.name: EmailListVerify
tools.what_it_does: Email verification with never-expiring pay-as-you-go credits — bulk list cleaning, real-time API, inbox-placement testing and free DMARC/SPF tools, plus a credit-based email finder.
tools.pricing: (2026) Pay-as-you-go credits that never expire: 1,000 for $5 ($0.005/check), 5,000 for $17, 10,000 for $27, 25,000 for $54, 50,000 for $98 ($0.00196/check). A monthly subscription saves ~10% vs pay-as-you-go; API included. The email finder costs 5 credits per found address. Free tools: email validator, inbox-placement test, DMARC/SPF generators.
tools.honest_knock: The $5 entry pack is the most expensive way to buy: $0.005 per check versus $0.00196 at the 50k tier — a 2.5x spread that rewards guessing your volume upfront. And the email finder quietly consumes 5 credits per found address, so a 1,000-credit pack finds 200 emails, not 1,000.
tools.best_for: teams cleaning real sending lists before campaigns — bulk verification at volume rates, with credits that never expire
tools.skip_if: you verify tiny batches occasionally (the entry rate is the worst per-check price), or you mainly want prospecting — the finder burns credits five at a time
compare_with: Bouncer leans into deliverability polish and EU data residency; EmailListVerify wins on raw per-check price at volume, with never-expiring pay-as-you-go credits

tools.name: Emergent
tools.what_it_does: AI app builder. Describe what you want and Emergent builds full-stack web apps for you — an agentic, credit-based platform that turns prompts into working software with no manual coding.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free $0 (10 credits/mo), Standard $20/mo (100 credits), Pro $200/mo (750 credits), Team $300/mo (1,250 shared credits); ~17% off annual. Credits meter the work: simple changes 1–2, medium features 5–10, complex refactors 10–20+.
tools.honest_knock: The real cost is credit consumption, not the flat sticker — a genuinely complex app burns 10–20+ credits per big change, so serious builders move up tiers faster than the price list implies. Now do the division, because Emergent's own pricing page doesn't. Standard is $20 for 100 credits, so 20 cents a credit. Pro is $200 for 750, which is 26.7 cents. Team is $300 for 1,250, or 24 cents. Moving up a tier makes every unit of work more expensive, not less: Pro costs 33% more per credit than Standard, and annual billing keeps the gap (17 cents against 22.3). That is the opposite of the volume discount the ladder looks like — you are buying seats, support and headroom, not cheaper work. Check what your month actually needs before you upgrade; two Standard months and a top-up may beat one Pro month. And AI-generated code still needs a human eye: review it for security, correctness and maintainability before anything touches real users. It's a superb way to go from prompt to working prototype or MVP fast; it's not a hands-off factory for production software.
tools.best_for: founders, PMs and builders who want to turn a prompt into a working full-stack web app or MVP fast, without writing the code themselves
tools.skip_if: you need a hardened, security-audited production system with no human review, or your usage would burn through credits faster than the value returns
compare_with: close AI app-builder rivals — compare credit economics and output quality on the kind of app you actually build

tools.name: Employment Hero
tools.what_it_does: Modular HR, payroll and recruitment platform for small and mid-size employers.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Sold as separate modules rather than one plan. Recruitment: a free ATS tier at $0, then $199, $359, $639 and $959 a month for 50, 100, 200 and 300 AI video interviews — their page notes no HR or payroll subscription is required for these. HR Essentials $10 per employee per month, HR Engage $14, Payroll $10. Chat is $2 per employee per month with a stated $20 a month minimum. Every price on the page carries an asterisk.
tools.honest_knock: There is no such thing as the Employment Hero price. HR, payroll, recruitment and chat are four separate subscriptions and three of them are per employee, so the number you want is a sum you have to build yourself. A twenty-person company on HR Engage plus Payroll is $14 plus $10 per employee, which is $480 a month before recruitment. The recruitment tiers are the odd one out: they are priced by AI video interviews rather than by people, so a hiring push moves that line independently of your headcount. And every figure on the page has an asterisk against it — find out what those say before you compare this with anything.
tools.best_for: small and mid-size employers who want HR and payroll from one vendor and will genuinely use both, where the per-employee rate beats separate systems
tools.skip_if: you only need one of the four modules — each is sold separately and priced as though you are buying the platform, so a dedicated payroll or ATS tool is usually cheaper on its own
compare_with: the usual comparison — build the total for the modules you actually need at your headcount, because the entry per-employee rate is only one of three or four lines

tools.name: EngageBay
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one CRM, marketing, helpdesk and live chat for small teams — a genuine free tier (250 contacts) and per-user suites that undercut the big names.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 16 Jul 2026) Genuinely free tier: $0 for 250 contacts with email marketing, CRM, helpdesk and live chat. All-in-One suite per user/month: Basic $14.99 (500 contacts), Growth $64.99 (5,000 contacts, marketing automation), Pro $119.99 (unlimited contacts) — note the pricing page defaults to biennial ‘15% off’ display (Basic shows $12.74, Growth $55.24, Pro $101.99), so toggle to monthly for the list price. Single bays (Marketing or CRM & Sales) from $11.04/user/mo on that same biennial display.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is contacts AND seats at once: prices are per user, and each tier caps contacts — Basic’s 500 contacts fills fast, and the Growth jump is steep ($15 → $65 per user). The advertised ‘starts at $12.74’ assumes biennial prepay — two years upfront for the friendly number. Real automation only starts at Growth.
tools.best_for: small teams that want CRM, email marketing, helpdesk and live chat in one affordable suite — the free tier is a genuine trial-for-life, and it undercuts HubSpot hard at small scale
tools.skip_if: your contact list is big (per-tier caps push you up fast) or you need best-of-breed depth in one area — all-in-one means good-at-everything, not best-at-anything
compare_with: Keap is the automation-first veteran at a higher price point; EngageBay is the budget all-in-one with a real free tier — pick Keap for automation depth, EngageBay for breadth per dollar

tools.name: Envoy
tools.what_it_does: Workplace platform for visitor sign-in, desk and room booking, deliveries and emergency notifications.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Five products, each metered differently and all billed annually. Visitors: Basic free, Premium $362 per location per month, Enterprise quote-only. Emergency Notifications $2 per user per month. Reservations $5 per bookable resource per month. Screens $12 per device per month. Deliveries $250 per delivery location per month. Every product section carries the line 'Price excludes platform fee', and the page never says what that platform fee is.
tools.honest_knock: None of the prices on that page is a price you can budget from, because every one of them is followed by 'Price excludes platform fee' and the fee has no number anywhere. That is the first thing to ask for. The second is how the meters stack, because they are all in different units: per location, per user, per bookable resource, per device, per delivery location. An office with forty bookable desks, six screens and one delivery point is paying on four clocks at once — $362 for the location, $200 for the desks, $72 for the screens and $250 for deliveries, which is $884 a month before the platform fee and before emergency notifications at $2 a head. Price the combination you actually want, not the product you came for.
tools.best_for: companies with a real office and a front desk problem — visitor compliance, desk booking and deliveries in one system, where the per-location price is spread over enough employees to be worth it
tools.skip_if: you are remote-first or have one small office — a visitor log and a shared calendar cover the same ground, and the per-location floor is priced for buildings rather than teams
compare_with: the direct workplace-platform peers — compare the total across every module you would switch on, and get all three to name their platform fee

tools.name: Evolve
tools.what_it_does: AI-native training and enablement platform for enterprises: an LMS with branded academies, an AI course generator, job-skill simulations with AI counterparts, an assessment center and performance analytics — used by 100+ deployed enterprises.
tools.pricing: (2026) No public price list — enterprise quote-based only ('book an intro'). The platform is modular (LMS, AI course generator, simulations, assessment center), so the quote depends on which modules and seat volume you contract; budget for an enterprise-tier commitment.
tools.honest_knock: It's built for large organizations — the site lists 100+ deployed enterprises like Carlsberg and Danone — and the sales-led, quote-only motion reflects that: there is no self-serve tier to trial quietly, so smaller teams can't just kick the tires before procurement gets involved.
tools.best_for: enterprises and scale-ups that need structured, measurable training rolled out across hundreds of employees — branded academies, AI-generated courses, job-skill simulations and assessment in one platform
tools.skip_if: you're a small team that just needs a course builder or a lightweight LMS — the enterprise machinery and the procurement process are more than the job requires
compare_with: the established enterprise-LMS names win on integration marketplaces and long track records; Evolve wins on AI-native course generation and built-in job simulations with AI counterparts

tools.name: Expandi
tools.what_it_does: LinkedIn and email outreach automation for sales teams and agencies — smart limits, warm-up and multi-account management.
tools.pricing: (2026) 7-day free trial, no free plan. Business $99/mo month-to-month, or $79/mo on annual billing (2 months free). Higher tiers add role and permission management and centralized billing; pricing scales with seats.
tools.honest_knock: There is no free tier and no cheap entry — Expandi starts at $99 a month per seat, and the friendlier $79 assumes annual commitment. It's also LinkedIn automation, which sits in a grey zone against LinkedIn's own terms: powerful for outreach, but a platform-risk you own.
tools.best_for: sales teams and agencies running LinkedIn (and email) outreach at scale who want smart sending limits, warm-up and multi-account management
tools.skip_if: you send occasional connection requests (LinkedIn's native tools suffice), or you're uneasy about automation against LinkedIn's terms of service
compare_with: lemlist is the multichannel outreach all-rounder with a big template community; Expandi is the LinkedIn-automation specialist — sharper for that channel, no free tier, and the usual platform risk

tools.name: ExpertEx
tools.what_it_does: A unified AI studio: chat across multiple models (GPT-4, Gemini), generate images, video and voice, and reuse prompts — multilingual, all in one workspace.
tools.pricing: A free arena lets you compare up to ~6 models; paid pricing isn't clearly published — check it before committing.
tools.honest_knock: Reviews are genuinely mixed (Trustpilot around 3.7) — start on the free model-comparison arena and confirm it fits your workflow before paying.
tools.best_for: teams comparing multiple AI models side-by-side before committing — the free arena for ~6 models is a genuinely useful evaluation tool
tools.skip_if: you need published, predictable pricing to budget on — paid tiers weren't clearly public at research time

tools.name: Expertise AI
tools.what_it_does: AI sales agent for B2B websites. Replaces a static chatbot with a live, RAG-grounded agent that holds buying conversations, qualifies visitors and routes them to reps or calendar slots — HubSpot-first, with visitor intelligence.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-07-21) Free Preview at no cost (1 AI agent, 10 conversations, up to 50 training materials), Growth $500/mo billed monthly or $400/mo billed yearly (1 agent, unlimited conversations, up to 500 training materials, HubSpot integration and live-chat handoff), Business $1250/mo on both monthly and yearly billing (visitor intelligence, proactive live chat in HubSpot, 2-way HubSpot sync, Voice AI, 3 playbooks, webhook, implementation by their team), Enterprise custom.
tools.honest_knock: The honest catch is the gap between tiers: Pro at $150 is accessible, but the features that make it genuinely powerful — visitor intelligence that de-anonymizes traffic, all integrations, advanced analytics — live on the $1,000 Business tier, a big jump. It's also a RAG agent, so it's only as good as the docs you feed it: give it thin content and it can answer buyers confidently but wrong. Strong for HubSpot-centric B2B teams; less compelling if you're not in that ecosystem.
tools.best_for: B2B software teams (especially HubSpot-first) that want a live AI sales agent to qualify website visitors, hold buying conversations and route leads to reps
tools.skip_if: you're not running B2B demand-gen through a CRM like HubSpot, or a simpler support chatbot covers your needs at a fraction of the Business-tier cost
compare_with: close conversational-sales/AI-agent platforms — Expertise AI leans HubSpot-first B2B; compare on visitor-intelligence features and tier pricing

tools.name: ExpertSender
tools.what_it_does: E-commerce marketing automation with a built-in customer data platform: email, SMS, web and mobile push plus on-site messages, behavior-triggered workflows, product recommendations and segmentation on unified store data.
tools.pricing: (2026) Quote-based with a documented floor: their site lists pricing starting around $450/mo, scaling with volume and channels, and they explicitly target stores with at least 30,000 unique monthly visits. No free tier — a free consultation is the entry point.
tools.honest_knock: The $450/mo floor and the 30k-monthly-visits target make this an established-store tool, not a starter one: below that traffic the platform can't pay for itself, and there is no self-serve plan to test it cheaply first.
tools.best_for: e-commerce stores from 10,000+ monthly visitors (the vendor's own stated ICP) and high-volume senders doing 100k+ emails a month, who want email, SMS, push and on-site messaging on one unified customer data platform with a managed, dedicated-partner setup
tools.skip_if: your store is still building traffic or you want self-serve, pay-as-you-grow email marketing — a Klaviyo-class tool is the lighter, cheaper start
compare_with: Klaviyo and Omnisend win on self-serve onboarding and ecosystem breadth for smaller stores; ExpertSender wins on managed service and a unified CDP for bigger catalogs

tools.name: Fastmail
tools.what_it_does: Private, ad-free email hosting with your own domain. Fast, secure email, calendars and contacts from an independent provider that doesn't mine your data. From 1 August 2026 you pick EU (Amsterdam) or US data residency, encrypted at rest on Fastmail's own servers — note that EU data is initially still replicated and backed up to the US while that infrastructure matures.
tools.pricing: (2026) Individual about $5/mo annual; Duo/Family tiers push per-person cost under ~$2.50; business per-user tiers: Basic $4, Standard $6, Professional $10/user/mo (up to 150GB/user). 30-day full trial, no card; multi-year prepay discounts.
tools.honest_knock: You're paying for what the free giants monetize differently: no ads, no profiling, real support and standards-first email (JMAP/IMAP everywhere). The honest limits: it's email/calendar/contacts, not a Workspace-style office suite, so document collaboration lives elsewhere, and migrating decades of Gmail habits (filters, integrations) takes a weekend of care. For owning your address on your own domain, it's the boring, excellent choice.
tools.best_for: individuals and small businesses that want fast, private, ad-free email on their own domain with proper support and masked-email aliases
tools.skip_if: your team lives in Google Docs/Drive collaboration (Workspace bundles that), or free mail genuinely serves you and privacy isn't a priority
compare_with: Proton leads on E2EE, Workspace on suite breadth — Fastmail wins on speed, standards support and price for pure email

tools.name: Feedvisor
tools.what_it_does: AI-driven Amazon and retail-media optimization: dynamic repricing, ad automation and analytics for brands and larger sellers on Amazon and Walmart.
tools.pricing: (2026) Essentials from about $100/mo (entry repricing for smaller catalogs); the real platform — Feedvisor360 with AI repricing, advertising optimization and dedicated support — starts around $1,500/mo. 14-day trial.
tools.honest_knock: The honest structure: the $100 tier is a limited on-ramp, and most of what Feedvisor is famous for (the algorithmic Buy-Box strategy that holds prices UP, ad management, analysts) lives behind the $1,500+ 360 tier — this is enterprise software for serious catalogs, priced accordingly. If your Amazon revenue can't absorb that as a small percentage, simpler repricers are the rational choice.
tools.best_for: mid-market and enterprise Amazon sellers with large catalogs where algorithmic repricing and ad optimization move real revenue
tools.skip_if: you're a small seller (rule-based repricers cost a tenth), or your margins are set by factors repricing can't touch
compare_with: the accessible repricer tier — far cheaper, rule-plus-AI based; Feedvisor's edge is holding price ceilings, not just winning races to the bottom

tools.name: Filevine
tools.what_it_does: Case management for law firms: matters, intake, depositions, e-signature and AI document work.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) No prices are shown. Their own wording: all packages are custom built for your team's needs. The page describes five products — LOIS (AI features), Matters, Intake, Depositions and Signatures — and routes everything to a sales team for a custom quote. No per-user cost, no minimum seats, no contract length and no implementation fee is published.
tools.honest_knock: Nothing is priced, so everything is negotiable — which cuts both ways. In legal software the number that usually surprises people is not the per-seat rate but implementation: data migration from your existing case system, template configuration and training, quoted separately and often as a one-off in the thousands. That figure is absent here along with everything else. Ask for it as its own line, ask what the contract length is, and ask what happens to your matter data if you leave. A custom quote is fine; a custom quote you cannot compare against a rate card is what you are trying to avoid.
tools.best_for: law firms past the point where a general project tool works, with enough matters that case-specific workflows and intake tracking pay back a negotiated annual contract
tools.skip_if: you are a small practice wanting a published price to compare — this category will not give you one, and simpler practice-management tools do publish theirs
compare_with: the standing comparison in legal case management — both publish per-user prices, which makes them the honest benchmark for whatever Filevine quotes

tools.name: Finale Inventory
tools.what_it_does: Inventory and warehouse management for e-commerce and wholesale: multi-channel stock sync, purchasing and barcode workflows that scale with order volume.
tools.pricing: Self-Starter around $99/mo (one user, up to ~500 orders/mo); mid-tiers roughly $200–$800/mo add multi-channel sync and advanced reporting; enterprise $1,000+/mo. Month-to-month or annual, no setup fees (2026).
tools.honest_knock: It's built for real warehouse volume, and the price reflects that — at $99 you're capped on orders and users, so a growing multi-channel seller climbs the tiers quickly. If you do a few dozen orders a month, this is more inventory engine, and cost, than you need. The interface is functional rather than flashy: you're buying depth, not polish.
tools.best_for: e-commerce and wholesale operations with real order volume that need multi-channel stock sync, purchasing and barcode-driven warehouse workflows
tools.skip_if: you're a low-volume store where your sales platform's built-in inventory is enough, or you want a slick modern UI over deep functionality
compare_with: comparable multi-channel inventory platforms — weigh by which sales channels and integrations you actually run

tools.name: Fireflies.ai
tools.what_it_does: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes and summarizes your calls across Zoom, Google Meet and Teams — searchable notes, action items and CRM sync, so nobody takes minutes by hand.
tools.pricing: Free plan with unlimited transcription (limited AI); Pro ~$10/seat/mo and Business ~$19/seat/mo in 2026.
tools.honest_knock: Paid tiers cap AI credits, and if you mainly want real-time in-Zoom captioning and simple English notes, Otter is the simpler pick.
tools.best_for: teams that want every meeting transcribed and searchable automatically — the free unlimited-transcription tier is genuinely rare
tools.skip_if: your meetings involve sensitive topics where an AI notetaker joining calls raises consent or confidentiality questions — check policy first

tools.name: FlexiQuiz
tools.what_it_does: Online quiz and test maker for educators, trainers and businesses: build graded exams, assessments and simple courses with certificates, timed tests, question banks and analytics — from a genuinely free tier.
tools.pricing: (2026) A genuinely free plan (up to 20 responses a month); paid tiers run roughly $17/mo (Essentials) to about $60/mo (Premium), with Enterprise above that (contact sales for Enterprise+). Annual billing saves 25%+. The response caps are the real ladder: roughly 500/month on Essentials versus 2,000 on Premium.
tools.honest_knock: The monthly response caps are the business model: 20 on free, roughly 500 on Essentials and 2,000 on Premium — one viral quiz or one big exam cohort and you're shopping a tier up. Price the cap you'll actually hit, not the sticker.
tools.best_for: educators, trainers and small teams that want professional graded quizzes, exams and simple courses — with certificates, timed tests, question banks and analytics — without building out a full LMS
tools.skip_if: you need a complete learning platform with deep integrations, or your volumes run past a few thousand responses a month — the caps make it the wrong shape
compare_with: the generic form tools win on price and ubiquity for simple surveys; FlexiQuiz wins on exam features — grading, certificates, timed tests and question banks

tools.name: Flippa
tools.what_it_does: The world's #1 marketplace to buy and sell online businesses, SaaS, apps, and domains. Turn your digital assets into liquid capital.
tools.pricing: Sellers pay a listing fee (about $29 for sub-$10k assets, rising to roughly $59–$699 for larger or premium listings) plus a success fee on sale that starts near 3% and scales with price; a brokered service for listings above ~$100k adds about $999. Buyers join free; escrow fees apply. Verify current fee tiers (2026).
tools.honest_knock: The real cost is the success fee, and it's a flat bracket rate on the whole sale price, not marginal — a mid-five-figure sale can hand over a four- to five-figure commission. Flippa is also a self-serve marketplace: more listings, but more due-diligence burden on you. Verification and quality vary, so buyers must vet hard and sellers should expect tyre-kickers. It's reach and liquidity, not a white-glove broker.
tools.best_for: buyers and sellers of small-to-mid online businesses, SaaS, apps and domains who want the largest marketplace and are comfortable doing their own due diligence
tools.skip_if: you're selling a large, premium business where a dedicated broker's vetting and negotiation earns its higher fee, or you want a hands-off sale
compare_with: brokered marketplaces that vet harder and charge more — better for larger, cleaner exits; Flippa wins on reach and low entry cost

tools.name: Flocksy
tools.what_it_does: A dedicated creative team for one flat monthly fee. Unlimited graphic design, video editing, motion graphics and web design — your marketing never waits on a freelancer again.
tools.pricing: Flat monthly plans priced by dedicated creative hours per business day: $1,199/mo for 2h/day, $1,699 (3h/day), $2,199 (4h/day), $2,599 (5h/day), $2,999 (6h/day), $3,399 (7h/day) and $3,799/mo for 8h/day, each billed annually and shown per month (re-verified 2026-08-06). Plans start at 2 daily hours and scale to 8, with custom teams beyond that; month-to-month costs more — on the 4h/day plan Flocksy prices annual billing as saving $10,800/yr versus monthly. The pricing page carries a money-back guarantee.
tools.honest_knock: 'Unlimited' means unlimited queue, not unlimited throughput: work happens at your plan's daily capacity, so a big launch week still needs planning, and turnaround expectations are where subscription-design relationships sour. The economics are simple and honest — against even one freelance designer's day rate, the math works IF you feed it steady volume; if your design needs are sporadic, a flat monthly fee is paying for silence.
tools.best_for: marketing teams and agencies with steady, recurring creative volume (ads, social, video edits) that want predictable flat-fee capacity instead of freelancer wrangling
tools.skip_if: your design needs are occasional or spiky (pay per project instead), or you need one senior specialist deeply embedded in your brand
compare_with: the unlimited-design subscription peers — compare real turnaround and daily capacity at equal price, not the 'unlimited' word

tools.name: folk
tools.what_it_does: Lightweight, collaborative CRM for managing contacts and relationships. Centralize your network and personalize outreach without the bloat. A mobile app (Contacts by folk) adds on-the-go search, one-tap contact capture with business-card scanning, voice notes and interaction tracking across WhatsApp, LinkedIn, email and calendar.
tools.pricing: $30/member/month on Standard, $60 on Premium and from $100 on Enterprise when billed monthly; billed yearly those drop to $24, $48 and from $80 per member per month — 20% off — for $288, $576 and $960 per member per year (re-verified 2026-08-06). 14-day free trial, no credit card required.
tools.honest_knock: Two real gaps: there's no mobile app (browser only — the #1 complaint), and no proper workflow automation on any plan, just trigger-based emails. Enrichment is capped (~500–1,000/mo) and email sequences need at least Premium.
tools.best_for: small sales teams, agencies and VC/partnership teams who want a clean, fast-to-set-up CRM with a great LinkedIn enrichment extension
tools.skip_if: you're a solo founder who needs your network on your phone, or you need real workflow automation and reporting — folk is lightweight by design

tools.name: Foxit
tools.what_it_does: Comprehensive PDF editor and e-signature solution. Edit, secure, and sign digital documents seamlessly as a lightweight alternative to Adobe Acrobat.
tools.pricing: (2026) PDF Editor about $129.99/yr (desktop + 20GB cloud); Editor+ ~$159.99/yr (adds mobile, AI redaction); monthly options ~$10.99-13.99/mo. eSign runs separately (~$120/yr individual, ~$300/yr business with 5-user minimum); an AI Assistant add-on is ~$49.99/yr. 60% education discount.
tools.honest_knock: Foxit's whole pitch is being the honest fraction of Acrobat's price, and it largely delivers — the catches are modular: e-signing is a separate subscription (with a 5-user minimum on the business tier), and the AI features are an add-on, so the 'full Acrobat replacement' basket costs more than the headline editor. Still typically well under Adobe; just price your actual basket, not the first line.
tools.best_for: individuals and businesses that want full PDF editing, OCR and organizing at a fraction of Acrobat's subscription — especially multi-seat deployments
tools.skip_if: you only read and occasionally annotate PDFs (free readers cover it), or your org is contractually deep in the Adobe ecosystem
compare_with: Acrobat is the incumbent at 2-3x the price; PDF-XChange undercuts further on Windows — Foxit balances polish, platform breadth and price

tools.name: Frase
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered SEO content writing and optimization. Research, outline, write, and optimize articles that rank — all in one place.
tools.pricing: A 7-day free trial (no card); Starter about $39/mo (10 articles), Professional $109/mo (40), Scale $299/mo (100) on annual billing, roughly 15-20% more monthly (2026). GEO/AI-visibility tracking is now included on all plans.
tools.honest_knock: The article quotas pinch if you publish at volume (overage docs bill each), and it's a research-and-optimization tool, not a magic ranking button — it speeds up briefs, it doesn't replace the writing or the backlinks.
tools.best_for: content teams and SEOs who want to speed up research, briefs and SERP-driven optimization in one workflow
tools.skip_if: you publish only occasionally — the monthly quota and subscription outweigh the time saved for a handful of articles

tools.name: FreshBooks
tools.what_it_does: Invoicing and accounting aimed at freelancers and service businesses, priced by billable clients.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) The prices shown are 90% off for three months. Lite $2.30 a month promotional, $23 regular, 5 billable clients. Plus $4.30 promotional, $43 regular, 50 billable clients. Premium $7 promotional, $70 regular, unlimited clients. Select is quote-only. Team members are $11 a month each on every tier, with 2 included on Select. Two add-ons sit in the fine print: Advanced Payments $20 a month and Payroll $40 a month plus $6 per user.
tools.honest_knock: Two things multiply the number you first see. The promotional rate is 90% off for three months, so Lite is $23 rather than $2.30 from month four. And the meter is billable clients, not invoices or revenue: Lite stops at five, which a freelancer with a handful of retainers passes in their first good quarter, and the step to fifty clients is $43. Then people cost extra on top at $11 each, so a two-person studio on Plus is $54 a month rather than $43. Payroll is a separate $40 plus $6 a head, which is the line most people miss when they compare this against a bookkeeping tool that includes it.
tools.best_for: freelancers and small service firms who bill time and want invoicing that chases payment for them — the client cap is generous enough at Plus for most one-person businesses
tools.skip_if: you have more than a handful of clients and only need invoicing — the client cap is what pushes you up the ladder here, and flat-priced invoicing tools do not care how many clients you have
compare_with: the standing comparison — FreshBooks is friendlier for service billing, the other two are stronger accounting; compare on post-promotional price plus your team count

tools.name: Freshchat
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered customer messaging from Freshworks: live chat and chatbots across your website, app, WhatsApp and Instagram, with a unified agent inbox and automation that deflects repetitive questions.
tools.pricing: A free plan for up to 10 agents; paid Growth about $19, Pro $49, Enterprise $79 per agent/mo billed annually (a little more monthly), with Freddy AI billed as a usage-based add-on (2026).
tools.honest_knock: The free tier is genuinely useful for small teams, but AI features and higher-tier routing sit behind paid plans and add-ons — and being part of the wider Freshworks suite means you'll be nudged toward the full platform.
tools.best_for: small-to-mid support teams that want live chat and messaging with a real free tier to start
tools.skip_if: you need a full help-desk and ticketing system, not just chat — look at a complete support suite instead of bolting on channels

tools.name: Freshservice
tools.what_it_does: AI-powered IT service management (ITSM) from Freshworks: cloud help desk, ticketing, asset management and workflow automation to run IT support and internal service desks without heavy ITIL overhead.
tools.pricing: Per-agent (2026): Starter about $19/agent/mo annual ($29 monthly), Growth ~$49 ($59), Pro ~$99 ($119), Enterprise custom. Monthly billing runs 35-50% higher; AI sessions, orchestration transactions and asset overages meter on top.
tools.honest_knock: The $19 headline rarely survives contact with a real deployment: the ITSM features most IT teams buy for (change/problem management, deeper analytics) live at Pro, and the modern extras — AI agent sessions, orchestration runs, asset counts — meter separately. Price the tier that contains your must-haves plus realistic AI usage, not the starter row. Within that honesty, it's one of the fastest ITSM tools to actually stand up.
tools.best_for: IT teams that want proper ITSM (incidents, assets, changes, service catalog) running in weeks, without enterprise-suite implementation pain
tools.skip_if: you need a simple shared helpdesk (Freshdesk-class is cheaper) or you're at the scale where ServiceNow's depth is genuinely required
compare_with: JSM undercuts for dev-centric teams; ServiceNow rules the enterprise — Freshservice wins the mid-market on speed-to-value

tools.name: Freshworks
tools.what_it_does: Suite of separately-sold products: Freshdesk support, Freshservice IT, Freshsales CRM, Freshchat and Freshcaller.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing pages) The main Freshworks pricing page carries no prices at all — it lists the products and links out to each one. On Freshdesk: Growth $19 per agent per month, Pro $55, Enterprise $89, all requiring annual billing, with a stated 20% annual saving and no monthly rate shown. Freddy AI Agent is included with the first 500 sessions. Freddy AI Copilot is a separate add-on at $29 per agent per month on Pro and Enterprise. Freshservice, Freshsales, Freshchat and Freshcaller are separate subscriptions with their own pricing pages.
tools.honest_knock: Freshworks is not a product, it is five of them, and the page you land on when you search for its price does not contain a price. Once you find Freshdesk's own page, two things sit on top of the number: the listed rates require an annual commitment, and Freddy AI Copilot — the AI the marketing leads with — is $29 per agent per month extra, which is 53% on top of a Pro seat. The Freddy AI Agent that is included stops after 500 sessions, with no published rate for what comes next. If you want support and IT and CRM, price three subscriptions, not one.
tools.best_for: teams who want a support desk that is cheaper per agent than the category leaders and will genuinely use the annual commitment — Growth at $19 is real value if ticketing is all you need
tools.skip_if: you want the AI-first product the marketing describes without doing the arithmetic, because that configuration is $55 plus $29 an agent; also skip it if you need month-to-month, since the published prices assume a year
compare_with: the standing comparison — price all three with the AI add-on switched on, because that is where they separate

tools.name: FullEnrich
tools.what_it_does: B2B contact enrichment with waterfall data. Find verified emails and direct phone numbers for prospects by combining 15+ data sources in one lookup.
tools.pricing: Success-based credits (2026): Starter about $29/mo (500 credits), Pro ~$55/mo (1,000); an email costs 1 credit, a mobile number 10 — and you only pay when verified data is FOUND. Credits roll over (3 months on monthly, 12 on annual); enterprise custom.
tools.honest_knock: The pay-on-success model is refreshingly honest, but note the 10x: phone numbers eat credits ten times faster than emails, so a calling-heavy motion consumes budget quickly — model your email/phone mix. As an orchestration layer over 15+ providers, its hit rate genuinely beats single databases; the flip side is you're paying a premium per contact versus querying one source that might have sufficed.
tools.best_for: outbound teams that need maximum find-rates on emails and especially mobile numbers, and prefer paying only for verified hits
tools.skip_if: you only need emails at volume (single-source tools are cheaper per hit), or your ICP data lives fine in one database already
compare_with: Clay orchestrates flexibly at platform prices; dedicated finders undercut on email-only — FullEnrich's edge is the waterfall hit-rate on phones

tools.name: Gamma
tools.what_it_does: A new medium for presenting ideas. Generate beautiful, interactive documents, decks, and webpages instantly with AI.
tools.pricing: Free (400 one-time AI credits, Gamma branding); Plus about $12/mo (~$9 annual, 1,000 credits/mo, no badge), Pro about $25/mo (~$18 annual, 4,000 credits), plus Team and Business tiers (2026).
tools.honest_knock: The credit model means heavy generation eats your monthly allowance, and outputs still need a human polish for high-stakes decks — it's a brilliant first-draft engine, not a finished-deck button. The free tier's watermark pushes you to paid quickly.
tools.best_for: anyone who wants to turn a prompt or notes into a good-looking presentation, doc or webpage draft in minutes
tools.skip_if: you need pixel-perfect, brand-controlled decks — you'll spend the saved time re-polishing the AI output
compare_with: other AI and template presentation tools

tools.name: Gelato
tools.what_it_does: Global print-on-demand platform: design, produce and ship custom products (apparel, wall art, mugs, photo books) locally in 30+ countries with no inventory — integrates with Shopify, Etsy and WooCommerce.
tools.pricing: (2026) A free plan ($0 forever) with core print-on-demand; Gelato+ is about $29.99/mo (or $19.99 annual) adding premium mockups, a stock-image library and year-round product discounts (up to ~25–35%); Platinum is custom for high volume. Gelato+ tends to pay for itself past ~10–20 orders/month.
tools.honest_knock: The free plan is genuinely usable, so the honest question is only whether Gelato+ earns its fee — and that depends entirely on volume: below ~10 orders a month the discounts won't cover the subscription. Its real edge is local production in 30+ countries (fast, cheaper international shipping), but that means quality and product availability can vary slightly by region and print partner. Sample your key products before scaling.
tools.best_for: creators and stores selling custom products internationally who want local production in many countries to cut shipping time and cost, with no inventory
tools.skip_if: you sell only a handful of orders a month (stay on the free plan) or your customers are concentrated in one country where a single-hub competitor is simpler
compare_with: the major POD alternatives — Gelato's differentiator is its global local-production network; compare product range and per-item cost for your catalog

tools.name: Geotargetly
tools.what_it_does: Geo-targeting toolkit — location-based redirects, content swaps, popups and personalization by country, state and city, priced by traffic volume.
tools.pricing: (2026) 14-day free trial. Six tiers by traffic volume: Dev $12/mo, Startup $24, Growth $49, Business $99, High Traffic $199, Enterprise from $349 — billed yearly that becomes $9/$19/$39/$79 and up. All plans include country, state and city-level targeting; visitor quotas scale per tier.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is your traffic: tiers gate on visitor quotas, so a growth spike pushes you up a tier whether you planned it or not — and the friendlier advertised numbers are the yearly-billing rates; month-to-month runs roughly a third higher.
tools.best_for: marketers personalizing redirects, content blocks and popups by visitor location — country to city level — without engineering work
tools.skip_if: your traffic is small enough for a hand-built redirect, or your CDN/edge stack already covers the basic geo-cases you need
compare_with: VWO is the full experimentation suite where geo is one dimension; Geotargetly is the geo-specialist — leaner and cheaper when location is the whole job

tools.name: GetResponse
tools.what_it_does: Powerful inbound marketing software combining email automation, landing pages, webinars, and conversion funnels.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-02, read on their own pricing page, in euros, quoted at 1,000 contacts) Free plan: 1,000 landing-page visitors a month, AI tools capped at 3 uses, webinars capped at 10 attendees, GetResponse branding retained, and premium features stop after 14 days. Starter €16/mo or €13.12/mo billed annually: 1 automation workflow, up to 3 users. Marketer €54/mo or €44.28 annual: unlimited workflows, 5 users, ecommerce tools, advanced segmentation, abandoned-cart recovery. Creator €62/mo or €50.84 annual: website builder, course creator up to 500 students, webinars up to 100 attendees. Enterprise quote-only, adding SMS, dedicated IP and 1,000-attendee webinars. Annual billing saves a stated 18%, and prices step up at 1k, 2.5k, 5k, 10k, 25k, 50k and 100k contacts.
tools.honest_knock: Priced by contact count, so the entry number climbs as your list grows, and the best value only shows on long (annual/24-month) commitments. A solid all-rounder, but you lock in to get the good rate.
tools.best_for: small businesses that want email plus landing pages, automation and webinars in one affordable suite
tools.skip_if: you only need basic broadcasts — a leaner tool costs less without the extra modules you won't use

tools.name: Getscreen
tools.what_it_does: Browser-based remote desktop and remote-support software: connect to any computer with no client install, share one-click access links, transfer files and record sessions — for IT teams, MSPs and remote support.
tools.pricing: Free plan (2 devices); paid tiers add one-time quick connections (Advanced) and white-label, roles and mass-device management (Enterprise) — plus a one-time Personal Lifetime Deal around $149, which sidesteps the recurring fees of rivals like TeamViewer (~$50/mo).
tools.honest_knock: AnyDesk tends to feel faster and lower-latency, and TeamViewer carries the heavier security/compliance certifications (HIPAA, SOC 2). Getscreen's real edge is being fully browser-based — nothing to install on the other person's machine — and cheaper, especially with the lifetime deal.
tools.best_for: IT and support people who want browser-based remote access without installing software on the other person's machine — at a fair price or a one-time fee
tools.skip_if: you need the absolute lowest latency (AnyDesk) or heavy compliance certifications like HIPAA/SOC 2 (TeamViewer)
compare_with: the faster and the more enterprise-secure rivals

tools.name: Glide
tools.what_it_does: No-code app builder that turns spreadsheets and databases into working business apps — internal tools, client portals and field apps, with workflows and an API.
tools.pricing: (re-verified 2026-08-04, read in a live browser session on both pricing pages, both tabs and both billing toggles) The classic spreadsheet-to-app builder still has a genuinely free tier — unlimited drafts, one editor, up to 25k rows — and its paid plans are unchanged, but they now live on glideapps.com/classic/pricing instead of the main pricing page. On the individual tab, Explorer starts at $19 per month billed yearly or $25 billed monthly (one app, 100 personal users, 250 updates, up to 25k rows) and Maker at $49 per month billed yearly or $60 monthly. On the business tab, Business starts at $199 per month billed yearly or $249 monthly, with unlimited apps, 30 users included, 5,000 updates and up to 100k rows; extra users are $5 each on annual billing and $6 on monthly, and extra updates cost 2 cents each. Enterprise is quote-only. VAT is added at checkout, and Business comes with a 14-day free trial. Glide now sells two products from two pages: what glideapps.com/pricing shows today is GlideOS, the newer AI builder, on its own separate subscription — Free with one project and limited credits, Solo at $25 per month with 5 projects and credit bundles from 100 to 10,000 per month, Team at $125 per month for 5 members with $10 per additional member and 50 credits included per member, and a quote-only Enterprise tier. Glide states that annual GlideOS plans are coming soon, so the GlideOS prices above are monthly only.
tools.honest_knock: Glide meters updates, not just seats, so your bill tracks how busy the app is rather than how many people own a licence — a write-heavy workflow can pass the included 5,000 updates and add 2 cents each without anyone changing plan. The jump from Maker to Business is also steep: $49 to $199 per month on annual billing, and the row ceiling only moves from 25k to 100k. Worth knowing too that the pricing above is for the classic Glide builder; GlideOS, the AI-era product Glide advertises on its own homepage, is a separate and newer thing, so do not assume a feature you saw demoed there is included in the plan you are buying.
tools.best_for: teams that already run operations out of spreadsheets and want a real app on top — internal tools, field data capture, client portals — without hiring a developer
tools.skip_if: you need heavy custom logic or a high-write consumer app: the update metering punishes exactly that shape of workload, and anything beyond the published ceilings is a quote-only conversation

tools.name: Goflow
tools.what_it_does: Multichannel e-commerce operations: orders, inventory, listings and shipping across all your marketplaces in one dashboard. Goflow Core is free and automates Amazon MCF fulfilment for TikTok Shop orders; the vendor states eligible orders may qualify for 35% savings on Amazon MCF rates (vendor mail, 27 Jul 2026). A nocnoc integration keeps Latin American listings, inventory, orders and fulfilment in sync from inside Goflow (vendor mail, 5 Aug 2026).
tools.pricing: (2026) A free Core plan to start; paid plans from about $499/mo, scaling with order volume and complexity (Launch/Scale/Enterprise) — every tier includes the full platform (orders, inventory, listings, shipping, automation). No setup fees, though EDI connections run a one-time ~$500-1,300 each.
tools.honest_knock: The all-features-on-every-tier model is refreshingly honest — you pay for volume, not unlocks — but the $499 floor means Goflow is for operations with real order flow, not side-project stores. The EDI setup fees per connection are the line item to budget when big-box retail is the goal; they're one-time, but they multiply by the number of retail partners.
tools.best_for: multichannel e-commerce operations with serious order volume that want orders, inventory, purchasing, listings and shipping unified — including EDI retail
tools.skip_if: you're under a few hundred orders a month (lighter tools cost a tenth), or you sell on one channel only
compare_with: the multichannel-ops peer set — compare at your order volume and count the EDI connections you'll actually need

tools.name: Gorgias
tools.what_it_does: Helpdesk built for ecommerce: tickets, automations and an AI agent, priced by volume rather than by seat.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Not priced per agent — their own line. Two meters that stack. Starter is $40/month all in: a $10/month helpdesk with 50 tickets included and $0.40 per ticket beyond, plus the AI Agent at $30/month with 30 automated interactions and $1.50 per interaction beyond. Basic is $90/month month-to-month or $77/month billed annually ($924 a year), including 300 tickets and 30 automated interactions, with the same $0.40 and $1.50 overage rates. Higher tiers scale the ticket allowance; their own framing is 50 to 5,000 tickets a month.
tools.honest_knock: Never priced per agent is a real advantage and worth saying plainly: your whole team can be in the inbox without the bill moving. The cost sits on two meters instead, and both bite. Tickets beyond your allowance are $0.40 each, so a bad week costs money rather than attention. And the AI agent — the thing the homepage leads with — is a separate $30 a month on the entry plan, which is three times the helpdesk it sits on, with automated interactions past 30 charged at $1.50 each. So the honest entry price for the product as advertised is $40, not $10. Count a normal month's tickets and a busy month's, and price both.
tools.best_for: ecommerce support teams with seasonal or spiky volume, where per-agent pricing punishes you for having enough people on a busy week
tools.skip_if: your volume is steady and low — 50 tickets a month is the entry allowance, and below that a shared inbox costs nothing; also skip the AI agent until you know your automated-interaction count, since that is the meter that runs away
compare_with: the standing comparison — Gorgias wins when your team is larger than your ticket volume suggests, and loses when your volume is high and steady

tools.name: GrapeLeads
tools.what_it_does: Lead-finding for web developers and agencies — surfaces local businesses without websites from Google Maps, with contact details, on signup credits.
tools.pricing: (2026) Credit-based, with 20 free credits at signup. At research time the site's own pricing link returned a 404 — there is no public price list; verify current credit-pack rates in-app before buying.
tools.honest_knock: The pricing page 404s: at research time the only public number was 20 free credits at signup. For a lead tool aimed at web professionals, a broken pricing page is an ironic look — check in-app rates before committing, and know that the niche (Google-Maps businesses without websites) is the real product.
tools.best_for: web developers, designers and agencies prospecting local businesses that do not have a website yet — surfaced from Google Maps with contact details
tools.skip_if: you sell to companies that already have an online presence, or you want transparent pricing before creating an account
compare_with: Bookyourdata sells verified B2B contact lists pay-as-you-go at published rates; GrapeLeads is the niche specialist for no-website local businesses — smaller pond, sharper spear

tools.name: Gravity Forms
tools.what_it_does: The gold standard in WordPress forms. Build advanced forms, surveys and workflows with conditional logic and hundreds of integrations.
tools.pricing: Annual WordPress licenses (2026): Basic about $59/yr (1 site), Pro about $159/yr (3 sites, payments), Elite about $259/yr (unlimited sites, all add-ons). Straightforward tiers by site count. Third-party add-ons (GravityView, Gravity Flow, Perks) can add roughly $99–349/yr.
tools.honest_knock: Two honest notes. It's a WordPress-only plugin — no WordPress, no Gravity Forms — and its real power often lives in paid add-ons and third-party extensions, so a genuinely advanced setup can cost more than the base license suggests. It's developer-friendly rather than beginner-slick; non-technical users may find hosted builders more polished. For a WordPress site, though, it's the reliable gold standard.
tools.best_for: WordPress site owners and developers who want powerful, self-hosted forms with conditional logic, payments and deep integrations they fully control
tools.skip_if: you're not on WordPress, or you want a hosted drag-and-drop builder with no plugin maintenance
compare_with: hosted SaaS builders that are slicker and platform-agnostic; Gravity Forms wins on WordPress control and a flat annual cost

tools.name: Guesty
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one management for short-term and vacation rentals: unify bookings, guest messaging, channel distribution and pricing across 60+ channels (Airbnb, Vrbo and more) in one dashboard.
tools.pricing: Guesty Lite is roughly $9/mo plus ~1% per reservation for 1–3 listings; Pro and Enterprise are custom-quoted (2026).
tools.honest_knock: Pricing runs higher than leaner rivals, onboarding has a learning curve, and some users flag support — it earns its keep at scale, but it's heavy for a single listing.
tools.best_for: hosts with 1-3 listings starting on Guesty Lite (~$9/mo + ~1% per reservation) who may grow into the full property-management platform
tools.skip_if: you want quote-free scaling — Pro and Enterprise are custom-priced, so growth means a sales conversation

tools.name: Gusto
tools.what_it_does: Payroll, benefits and HR in one friendly platform. Automated tax filings, employee onboarding and time tracking — run payroll for your whole team in just a few clicks.
tools.pricing: Simple about $49/mo base + $6/employee, Plus $80 + $12/employee, Premium $180 + $22/employee; a contractor-only plan from about $35 + $6/contractor (2026). US-focused.
tools.honest_knock: The base-plus-per-employee model is transparent but adds up, and Gusto is US-only — excellent for straightforward US payroll and benefits, but not the pick for international teams or complex multi-entity HR.
tools.best_for: US small businesses that want genuinely easy full-service payroll, benefits and tax compliance in one place
tools.skip_if: you employ people outside the US or need enterprise, multi-entity HR — Gusto is built for US SMB payroll

tools.name: Healthie
tools.what_it_does: All-in-one practice management and EHR for health, wellness and nutrition providers: scheduling, telehealth, secure messaging, billing and a branded client portal — plus a full API (GraphQL + webhooks) for automation. Built to scale with group practices.
tools.pricing: Tiered and it climbs: entry plans from ~$49/mo, mid-tiers around $129–149/mo, and group/enterprise plans scale with team size into four figures a month. Full API access sits above the standard group tier; 14-day free trial (2026).
tools.honest_knock: Two honest limits: it's pricier than alternatives with thin mid-tier options, and several users report slow customer service (sometimes a week or more to reply). It really only pays off at scale — solo or tiny practices get more value, more simply, elsewhere.
tools.best_for: growing group practices (10+ clinicians) in health, wellness and nutrition that need multi-provider scheduling, telehealth and a real API to automate operations
tools.skip_if: you're a solo practitioner or tiny team who wants the simplest, cheapest setup — SimplePractice is easier and lighter for that
compare_with: the simpler, cheaper solo-focused rival — but with no API

tools.name: Heard
tools.what_it_does: Done-for-you bookkeeping and taxes built for therapists and a growing range of health-and-wellness practices — SLPs, dieticians, chiropractors, audiologists, coaches, massage and physical therapists: monthly books, quarterly tax estimates, annual filing and S-corp support by specialists who know the niche.
tools.pricing: (2026) Annual billing only: Lite about $129/mo (monthly done-for-you bookkeeping + quarterly tax estimates; annual tax filing NOT included — a ~$750 one-off), Essential ~$169/mo (adds personal tax prep and filing), Premium ~$255/mo (S-Corps and group practices, business filing). Payroll is an add-on at $39/mo + $6/person; catch-up bookkeeping runs ~$99/month.
tools.honest_knock: Mind the fine print between tiers: the entry plan does not include your annual tax filing (a ~$750 one-off on Lite), it is annual billing only, and messy back-months cost extra as catch-up fees. Price the tier that actually includes filing.
tools.best_for: therapists and health-and-wellness practice owners — SLPs, dieticians, chiropractors, audiologists, coaches, massage and physical therapists — who want books, quarterly estimates and filing handled by specialists who know their niche
tools.skip_if: you are comfortable doing your own books in a general tool at a fraction of the price, or your business sits outside the health-and-wellness practice niche
compare_with: Bench wins on general small-business bookkeeping breadth, a good local CPA on complex situations; Heard wins on therapy-practice specialization and S-corp guidance

tools.name: Hello Bar
tools.what_it_does: Popup and notification-bar tool for lead capture: sticky bars, popups, slide-ins and full-screen takeovers that turn visitors into subscribers — with A/B testing, targeting rules and 20+ email-tool integrations.
tools.pricing: (2026) A free version and trial exist; paid tiers scale by monthly popup VIEWS — sources list Growth around $29-39/mo (~50k views), Premium ~$49-69/mo (~150k) and Elite ~$99-129/mo (~500k). Reported prices vary between sources, so verify current tiers on their pricing page.
tools.honest_knock: The meter is views, not results: every visitor who sees a popup counts against your quota, so a traffic spike raises the bill regardless of how many emails you actually captured — a busy site outgrows the entry tier fast. And the honest fundamental of every popup tool: it amplifies an offer, it doesn't create one. A weak lead magnet with a beautiful popup is still a weak lead magnet, and aggressive full-screen takeovers can cost more goodwill (and Core Web Vitals) than they capture.
tools.best_for: content sites, blogs and stores that already have traffic and a genuinely worthwhile offer, and want sticky bars, popups and slide-ins with A/B testing to convert more of that traffic into subscribers
tools.skip_if: your traffic is still small (fix distribution first — a popup on 200 visitors captures almost nothing), or your list-building runs through gated content and landing pages rather than on-page interrupts
compare_with: close popup-tool rivals — compare the view-quota math at your real traffic level, since that's what you're actually billed on

tools.name: HiBob
tools.what_it_does: Modern HR platform (Bob): HRIS, onboarding, time-off and people analytics for growing companies that want culture-first HR without enterprise bloat.
tools.pricing: Quote-only, per-employee-per-month with modules — there's no public price list; third-party estimates cluster in the mid-teens per employee/month plus a one-off implementation fee (roughly 10-20% of annual), but it's negotiated (2026). Get it in writing.
tools.honest_knock: Opaque pricing and an implementation fee mean the real cost only surfaces in a sales call — and it's built for scaling mid-size companies, so it's heavy and expensive for a small team.
tools.best_for: growing mid-size companies (roughly 50-500 staff) that have outgrown spreadsheets and want a modern, culture-focused HRIS
tools.skip_if: you're under about 25 employees — a lighter, transparently priced HR tool covers you without the implementation project
compare_with: simpler, more transparently priced HR platforms

tools.name: Hive
tools.what_it_does: Project management and team collaboration in one workspace. Plan projects, assign tasks and centralize communication so work keeps moving.
tools.pricing: (2026) Free tier (10 members); Starter about $5/user/mo annual ($7 monthly); Teams ~$12/user/mo annual ($18 monthly); Enterprise custom. Watch the add-ons: proofing, timesheets, goals, resourcing, analytics and automations each run ~+$5/user/mo.
tools.honest_knock: The seat price is honest bait, the add-on grid is the business model: switch on three add-ons and your $12 seat becomes $27 — a la carte flexibility that punishes teams who need the full toolkit. List your must-have modules first and compare the DRESSED price against all-inclusive rivals; for teams needing only core PM, though, Hive is genuinely cheap and pleasant.
tools.best_for: project teams that want flexible PM (Gantt, Kanban, forms, chat) and only pay for the modules they actually use
tools.skip_if: you need most of the add-ons anyway (all-inclusive tools price better), or your org demands one standardized suite
compare_with: the PM heavyweights — ClickUp bundles more per dollar, Asana wins polish; Hive wins if your module list is genuinely short

tools.name: Hopp
tools.what_it_does: Digital business cards and smart networking for teams. Share contact details instantly and capture leads, with branded cards your whole team can use.
tools.pricing: A free tier exists (2026); public pricing beyond that is fragmented across Hopp-branded products — verify the exact product and current plans on their site before committing.
tools.honest_knock: The honest note is brand confusion: multiple products share the Hopp name (Wix's link-in-bio tool among them), so make sure the thing you're evaluating is the digital-card/networking product you mean — and given thin public pricing, get current rates in writing. Digital cards themselves are a proven, low-cost category; the durable value is contact-sync into your CRM, not the tap-to-share moment.
tools.best_for: teams that want modern digital business cards with centralized branding, starting free and verifying paid tiers directly
tools.skip_if: you need a battle-tested team deployment today with published pricing (Blinq-class tools publish theirs)
compare_with: the established digital-card players with clear published pricing — compare CRM integrations and team admin at your size

tools.name: Hostinger
tools.what_it_does: Affordable, fast hosting with an AI website builder built in. Free domain, free SSL and 24/7 support — perfect for founders launching their first MVP or side project.
tools.pricing: Budget hosting: shared and WordPress from about $2.69/mo on long (24-48 month) terms, cloud from $3.59/mo, VPS from $5.84/mo (2026) — but renewals jump sharply (Premium ~$10.99, Business ~$16.99/mo).
tools.honest_knock: The headline price only holds if you prepay years up front — renewals run several times the intro rate, the number-one complaint. Budget for the renewal, and be realistic that budget shared hosting isn't managed-grade performance.
tools.best_for: budget-conscious owners and side projects that want cheap, decent hosting and will prepay a multi-year term
tools.skip_if: you run a business-critical, high-traffic site — the renewal jump and shared-tier limits make managed hosting the better long-run value

tools.name: Housecall Pro
tools.what_it_does: Field service management for home-service businesses. Schedule jobs, dispatch techs, send quotes and invoices, and take payments from one app.
tools.pricing: Basic about $59/mo (1 user, no GPS or QuickBooks), Essentials about $149/mo (up to 5 users), MAX about $299-329/mo; extra users ~$35/mo each, plus card processing around 2.59% (2026).
tools.honest_knock: The Basic tier is a trap for real field teams — it omits GPS tracking and QuickBooks sync, so most businesses need Essentials or up, and add-on users plus processing fees push the true cost higher. Price the tier you'll actually need.
tools.best_for: home-service businesses (HVAC, plumbing, cleaning) that want scheduling, dispatch, invoicing and payments in one app
tools.skip_if: you're a solo operator who just needs simple invoicing — the field-service features are more than you'll use

tools.name: Hubstaff
tools.what_it_does: Time tracking with screenshots, activity levels, GPS and payroll integration for distributed teams.
tools.pricing: (2026-08-01, read on their own pricing page) Priced per seat. Their own worked example puts the Team plan at $10 per seat per month. Their FAQ is explicit about what a seat means: 'Hubstaff charges per seat. This means that even if only two out of your three team members are using its tracking features, you will still have to pay for all three members.' Seats added mid-term on an annual plan are prorated — their example is $60 for a seat added in July on a January-to-December plan. Monthly and annual options exist, with different proration rules, and add-ons are available on lower tiers.
tools.honest_knock: The seat definition is the whole story and they state it plainly, which deserves credit: you pay for every seat you have created, not every person actually being tracked. So an account that grew with your headcount and never got tidied up is billing you for people who left. Audit your seat list before renewal, not after. The second thing is that features on the lower tiers are add-ons rather than inclusions, so the plan you priced and the plan that does what you watched in the demo may not be the same one. And be clear with yourself about why you are buying it: screenshots and activity levels change how a team feels about their work, and that cost does not appear on any pricing page.
tools.best_for: agencies and distributed teams that bill clients for hours and need defensible time records — the proof is the product, and per-seat is fair when every seat is a person you invoice for
tools.skip_if: you want to know whether your team is working — that is a management problem and surveillance software makes it worse; also skip it if seats churn a lot, since you pay for every seat you forget to remove
compare_with: the direct time-tracking peers — both are cheaper and neither takes screenshots by default, so decide first whether you actually need the monitoring

tools.name: Iconosquare
tools.what_it_does: Deep social media analytics and reporting for agencies and brands. Track performance, schedule content, and monitor competitors.
tools.pricing: (2026) A free plan (1 user, 2 profiles), then Launch around €33/mo, Scale around €69/mo and Excel from about €116/mo (white-label, API, dedicated CSM); roughly 17% off annual, custom for enterprise.
tools.honest_knock: Its depth is strongest on Instagram and the core networks; if your priority platform sits outside its best-supported set, coverage thins. Analytics is where it shines — scheduling and community features exist but aren't always as deep as dedicated publishers. And the per-seat, per-profile tiering means agencies managing many brands climb toward the Excel tier quicker than the headline Launch price suggests.
tools.best_for: agencies and brands that want deep social analytics, reporting and competitor benchmarking alongside scheduling, especially Instagram-first teams
tools.skip_if: you need a heavy-duty publishing workhorse across many niche platforms, or a single free native analytics view already answers your questions
compare_with: Sprout is a pricier all-in-one, Later is scheduling-first — Iconosquare's edge is analytics depth per dollar

tools.name: iContact
tools.what_it_does: Straightforward email marketing for growing businesses. Build campaigns and automations with drag-and-drop design and deliverability support.
tools.pricing: No permanent free plan any more — a 30-day free trial, then paid tiers by contact count: at 500 contacts, Standard $9/mo (templates, landing pages, automations) and Premium $16/mo (unlimited users, social posting, AI content assistant), plus custom for large lists. Pay yearly to save 15% (re-verified 2026-07-19).
tools.honest_knock: Pricing feels a touch high for what you get, and the Standard plan's hard caps on automations and landing pages push growing teams to upgrade sooner than expected. It's also less cutting-edge on automation than ActiveCampaign — its real edge is simplicity, strong deliverability and the included human support.
tools.best_for: small businesses and nonprofits who want a simple, reliable email tool with strong deliverability and a real marketing advisor included on every paid plan
tools.skip_if: you need advanced multi-branch automation (ActiveCampaign does more) or you're chasing the rock-bottom cheapest option

tools.name: IDrive
tools.what_it_does: Automated disaster recovery and cloud backup. Securely mirror unlimited devices to the cloud to protect against ransomware.
tools.pricing: (2026, re-verified 26 Jul 2026) Free 10 GB Basic tier. IDrive Mini is $0.25/month for 100 GB ($0.83/month for 500 GB). IDrive Personal is $9.99/month for 5 TB, shown discounted to $6.99/month with annual billing (save 30%), scaling up to $99.99/month ($69.99 discounted) at 100 TB. Team starts at the same $9.99/month ($6.99 discounted) for 5 computers and 5 users on 5 TB; Business starts at $19.99/month ($13.99 discounted) for 500 GB with unlimited users. Add-ons: server backup $5/month/server, and Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace backup at $20/seat/year. The honest catch is on the pricing page in IDrive's own words: the discounted price applies to the first year, standard pricing applies from year two.
tools.honest_knock: The first-year price is a teaser and the renewal is the price — IDrive says so itself under the plan table, and on the current numbers the step from discounted to standard is about 43% (Personal 5 TB goes from $6.99 to $9.99 a month). Budget on year-two rates, not the banner. Beyond that, the honest backup fundamentals apply: a backup you never test-restore is a hope, not a backup, and the first full backup of multi-TB data takes weeks over the wire unless you use their physical Express seed shipping.
tools.best_for: individuals and small businesses that want cheap multi-device cloud backup with versioning, snapshots and physical seed/restore shipping
tools.skip_if: you need real-time sync-and-collaborate storage (that's Drive/Dropbox territory, not backup), or you won't tolerate the year-two renewal jump
compare_with: Backblaze is simpler flat-rate per computer; Acronis adds security suites — IDrive wins on multi-device flexibility per dollar, as long as you price in the year-two step-up

tools.name: InboxAlly
tools.what_it_does: Email deliverability tool that trains your sender reputation: engagement-based signals keep your campaigns and cold outreach out of spam and in the primary inbox — works alongside any ESP or email platform.
tools.pricing: (2026) Starter about $149/mo (100 seed emails/day, 1 sender profile), Plus about $645/mo (500/day, 5 profiles), Premium about $1,190/mo (1,000/day, 10 profiles, strategy sessions); Enterprise custom. 10-day free trial, no card.
tools.honest_knock: This is a premium, seed-list-based deliverability tool, and the price reflects it — Starter alone is well above casual warm-up apps, so it only makes sense if inbox placement is genuinely costing you real revenue. It improves sender reputation through engagement signals, but it's not a magic fix for bad content or a purchased list: deliverability still depends on how you actually send. Buy it when the math (lost revenue from spam-foldering) clearly beats the monthly fee.
tools.best_for: serious senders — email marketers and cold-outreach teams — whose deliverability problems are costing measurable revenue and who need active reputation repair
tools.skip_if: you're a small sender who just needs basic list hygiene (cheaper warm-up tools suffice), or your inbox issues stem from content and list quality you haven't fixed
compare_with: lower-cost warm-up alternatives — InboxAlly is pricier and more hands-on; justify it by the revenue your spam-foldered mail is losing

tools.name: Increff
tools.what_it_does: Enterprise omnichannel inventory and supply chain management. Optimize your merchandising with intelligent algorithms.
tools.pricing: No public pricing page and no flat fee: Increff prices every deal case by case, scaled to the operation (warehouses, users and the modules you take — WMS, merchandising). Confirmed to us directly by Increff's partnership team on 28 Jul 2026. There are no published tiers to compare, so budget for an enterprise implementation and ask for a tailored quote.
tools.honest_knock: This is enterprise omnichannel supply-chain software, and the opaque, quote-based pricing signals the target customer: retail brands with real scale, not small stores. The value — algorithmic merchandising and inventory optimization — only pays off at a catalog and volume large enough for those optimizations to move money. For a small or mid seller, it's likely more platform (and cost and implementation) than the problem warrants. For a scaling omnichannel brand, it's built for exactly that.
tools.best_for: retail brands and omnichannel sellers at real scale needing warehouse management plus algorithm-driven merchandising and inventory optimization
tools.skip_if: you're a small or single-channel store where simpler inventory software suffices, or you can't commit to an enterprise implementation
compare_with: comparable inventory/warehouse platforms — Increff leans algorithmic merchandising for scaled retail; get quotes and weigh implementation

tools.name: Insightful
tools.what_it_does: Workforce analytics and productivity monitoring — time tracking, workflow optimization and insider-threat detection, priced per seat.
